Objective is to determine legal framework around window shopping (price and ETA extractions) for specific country. ** criminal punishment scope for specific country
** civil punishment scope for specific country 
** competitor T&C review
** etc
* Country legal council uses answers to questionnaire to define punishment scope for each window shopping scenario in the [+global risk matrix+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_eWb4mN9Nph8g1OuD0urnNoYmaPGjHEwlKYIMw3KfCU/edit]:

Hi [~accountid:60868d705426330072b4b6e2] - thanks for reaching out on this and helping to sort last week. Clearly there’s a need for teams to align on a new global process of what information should be displayed and where (and why) - I’m keen to be involved in sorting this for everyone.

The problem we need to solve for (globally) is *_where_* *collated local information on fare components can and should be displayed on our website*: there is a need to provide component specific information to platform users when it is not displayed in the app in a readily accessible manner. 

^This sort of granular or readily changing information cannot, for compelling practical and legal reasons, be displayed within T&Cs themselves. For reference only, those reasons include the following:

* (1) T&Cs need to apply uniformly to all users within a country (i.e. one document that everyone can use and refer to). It’s the nature of our business that some fare and/or timing components change based on a region or locality - this information is not available in the app (which has fixed global parameters). Referring to local specific information on the website solves this problem.
* (2) This information can change rapidly (i.e. we launch in a new locality and have to add new fees to our list of tolls). We need to give users up to 15 days' notice to change aspects of out T+Cs, which is too slow and cumbersome for the sake of, for example, just adding one new fee to a list. Again, referring to local specific information on the website solves this problem.
* (3) T&Cs cover a wide range of subjects and are meticulously drafted for maximum enforceability (often at the expense of being an easy read). The language within them is cold, short and full of complex references dealing with fringe and unlikely events (such as users that extract our intellectual property). They are necessarily very long, relatively speaking - again, they also apply to all localities. When passengers want to understand their fares, which again may vary locally, it is not a very user-friendly experience to refer them to such a complicated, all-encompassing document. Again, referring to local specific information on the website solves this problem.

So this information needs a home on our website *_somewhere_*_._ As it is, there’s been ongoing reliance globally on this sort of information being hosted on the FAQ pages, probably because the necessary information has already been set out onto them (rightly or wrongly). As per your comments, it’s clear that your team wants to avoid this practice going forward, which is fine but we do need an alternative home for this info (again, globally). Your team’s support in this interim period is appreciated 👍 

Whatever the long-term solution is, it is worth mentioning that platform users will be always be entitled to rely on *_all_* information hosted on our website whether it’s in our T&Cs, FAQs or somewhere else entirely. So there’s always going to be an ongoing need for all available information on our website to be up-to-date and correct.

I suggest we jump on a call this week to discuss further - I’ll reach out on slack to sort 👌

Hi Michael! 👋

Can this additional information (such as fares) be stored in the same place where the rest of the legal documents are - just not within the T&C document itself?

This is the approach for Car-sharing legal documents:

* There are Bolt Drive T&Cs - there’s no global T&C, as some markets have separate T&Cs (e.g. [+France+|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/441tYP1pIV4JBg2R9rgl1a/792fcc76b6e28a795c8ca2df10889d61/FR-_Bolt_Drive_TsCs_15_11_2022_VFIN.pdf]+,+ [+Estonia & Latvia+|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-bolt-drive/]);
* There are Bolt Drive Lists of Penalties and Additional Fees - again, stored differently in each market (one [example|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/5Au1TP0ZLt0PDn3rL1XYay/a3642b8f665568692c2017b5782c0dd4/20220926_Bolt_Drive_fines_and_additional_fees_EN__1_.pdf], another example for [+France+|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/441tYP1pIV4JBg2R9rgl1a/792fcc76b6e28a795c8ca2df10889d61/FR-_Bolt_Drive_TsCs_15_11_2022_VFIN.pdf] where the Penalties list is incorporated in T&C).

That way, changes in Penalties lists don’t require changes in the T&C itself (except for the French market, which has both types of documents combined into one, I’m not aware why they chose to do it this way though).

Either way, as we already agreed in last week’s discussions,  Help Center is not a suitable place for this information. Historically, we stored such information in Help Center, but this is not the approach we’ll go forward with anymore.

Resolution:

We take eater’s history by querying {{user_order_history}} service to get a list of order_ids for a user_id.

From our investigations, it seems that {{taxify_user_order_history.order_history_delivery}} is containing data from LIVE until {{2023-04-11 03:01:36.0 UTC}}, while our {{taxify_delivery_order.order}} table is containing data from LIVE until {{2023-04-09 22:58:42.0 UTC}}. This discrepancy cause some weird behaviours in prelive: when we create a new order in prelive, it will increment the latest order_id we find in our {{taxify_delivery_order.order}} PRELIVE database. Since it's {{order_id}} is behind {{user_order_history}}'s one, when we finish the order, the corresponding existing entry (which is actual data from LIVE) from {{taxify_user_order_history.order_history_delivery}} is updated with data from our tables. This can cause problems, since some fields (such as user_id) are not updated, thus the history may not be displayed for some users.

Hi [~accountid:60f2a71843c956007065f2ad] and [~accountid:61268a40129802006ae93f05] 

Thanks for raising your concerns - let me offer some additional explanation.

When we receive requests like this, we are not by default required to respond and provide the data requested (even if they threaten a fine). As we are subject to numerous different laws, we need to assess the requirements set out by the other laws we are subject to - in this case privacy laws - to determine if we have a legal basis to disclose the data and are satisfied that the data requested is proportionate/strictly necessary. This is very important because we need to demonstrate that we’ve taken steps to assess the scope of the request and in the absence of obtaining the consent of all of the impacted individuals' to disclose their data, we have another lawful basis to legitimise the disclosure of the data. 

In this instance, it is my view that we do not have enough information to assess the grounds of the request and the request itself is excessive in nature (as was also flagged by external counsel in their advice). I would need the police to provide additional information and/or narrow the scope of their request (in time/date). 

Responsibility for our approach to responding to these types of requests sits with my team and ultimately myself as Head of Privacy. If you would prefer, my team can reach out to the officer directly to discuss and explain our reasoning or I’m comfortable for you to send from a generic CS department email - let me know your preference. 

Thanks

Sam

Query used by Laur:


{noformat}WITH payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx AS (select
       creation_date,
      psp_reference,
      merchant_reference,
      payment_method,
      type,
      ssc.code as country_code,
      ssc.name as country_name,
      lower(sdr.gross_currency) as gross_currency,
      lower(net_currency) as net_currency,
      gross_credit_gc_,
      net_credit_nc_,
      batch_number,
      merchant_account,
      cast(split_part(sdr.booking_date, ' ', 1) as date) as booking_date,
      coalesce(sdr.gross_credit_gc_ / r.rate, 1) AS gross_credit_amount_eur,
      case when gross_currency IN('UAH') THEN 0.012
        when gross_currency IN('CZK', 'DKK', 'AUD', 'GBP', 'PLN', 'RON', 'SEK', 'ZAR', 'NOK', 'EUR') then 0.006
        else 0.015 end adyen_fx_markup,
      case when gross_currency !=  net_currency then TRUE else FALSE end is_currency_conversion
      --from glue.commerce_finance.payment_report_adyen_settlement_details_report_raw sdr
      FROM glue.finance_reports.adyen_settlement_report sdr
      JOIN glue.ng_public.admin_system_country ssc  on lower(sdr.gross_currency) = ssc.currency
      JOIN glue.ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r
            ON lower(sdr.gross_currency) = r.currency and cast(split_part(sdr.booking_date, ' ', 1) as date)= date (r.valid_on)
       )
SELECT
    extract(month from date(payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.booking_date)) as "payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.booking_date_month",
    payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.gross_currency  AS "payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.gross_currency",
    payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.is_currency_conversion  AS "payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.is_currency_conversion",
    COALESCE(SUM(payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.gross_credit_amount_eur ), 0) AS "payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.gross_credit_amount_eur",
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.gross_currency != payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.net_currency THEN payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.gross_credit_amount_eur*payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.adyen_fx_markup ELSE NULL END ), 0) AS "payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.fx_markup_amount_eur"
FROM payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx
WHERE payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.type = 'Settled' AND payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.is_currency_conversion --) = 'true'
		and date (payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.booking_date) >= date '2023-03-01' and date(payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.booking_date) < date '2023-04-01' 
GROUP BY
    extract(month from date(payment_reconciliation_adyen_fx.booking_date)),
    2,
    3
ORDER BY
    4 DESC{noformat}

Hello Lise,

In Hungary driver must use a taximeters for calculating the ride price and that is the official measuring tool while the application is being only the secondary measuring tool.

Due to this, drivers are entitled to change the ride price in the application when a ride is finished because in cases where app price alters from taximeter’s price driver need to adjust the price in the app.

This function is useful and ensures drivers align with legislation but some drivers tend to abuse this function in case of in-app payment rides. 

For example they take foreign people to the airport who are in a rush and don’t wait for the driver to finalize the ride in the application and set the price and don't check the price in the taximeter either. Some drivers in these cases set a higher price (+5-10%) in the application because there is a small chance that the rider will notice the difference. We saw behavior patterns like that in the past so it would be great if we had an overview regarding this which we could use to effectively investigate these abuses.

The current process is not faulty. We haven’t just covered one scenario which might happen. Even if CS does not issue a refund after the user has been charged a fine (*correctly*), it is not a faulty process. Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] 

here are our answers with respect to FRANCE. 

# *Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied?* 

No (Under French law, any person registered as a professional is presumed to be an independent contractor and not an employee. This presumption may be reversed if the existence of an employment relationship is successfully demonstrated before the courts).

*2. Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)*

Yes, Freenow has been audited in and investigated for ‘serious undeclared work’ (_travail dissimulé aggravé_) by the FR Social Security and Contributions Authority (URSSAF) and Labour Inspector in 2022. The suspicions were dismissed for lack of evidence. We were told that the same audit/investigation was carried out against Uber last year but might have been delayed (or suspended) due to irregularities. It is possible that Bolt may face similar audit/investigation in the future though there is currently no indication that this would happen this year. 

*3. Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria?*   

In the event of a dispute over the nature of the contract, there is a rebuttable presumption of non-employment. The contract is deemed to be a service agreement unless it is evidenced otherwise in court. Despite the name and the content of the contract entered into between the parties, the Labour court can rule that a contractual relationship has to be deemed  an employment contract, if the following criteria/ elements are fulfilled :

* the provision of work, 
* the payment of a remuneration, and 
* the existence of a ‘relationship (or link) of subordination’ -  which doesn’t have a legal definition under FR law, but it was described by the FR Supreme Court in a landmark ruling of 1996 as ‘the performance of work under the authority of an employer who has the power to give orders and  instructions, to control their execution and to sanction any breach by his subordinate’.  

The court will consider the actual _de facto_ relationship between the parties. The assessment is made on a case-by-case basis. 

*4. Are reclassification sensitive activity expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?*

The Labour Court will evaluate the actual relationship between the parties on a base-by-case basis to determine whether or not a subordination link is established between the parties.

Case law refers to multiple and non hierarchized factual elements, which can establish a subordination link. For instance, the following factual elements have been considered as indications of a relationship of subordination:

* any element showing the platform’s power of control, management and (direct and/or indirect) sanction towards the driver, such as the existence of orders/directives and a system of sanctions in case of inexecution;
* the existence of fixed work days and hours;
* the provision of means to perform the work;
* the existence of a uniform and/or elements suggesting that the independent contractor is a member of the company;
* the lack of freedom in developing their own business customers;
* prices imposed by a platform;

These elements are only indicative and it is not possible to be comprehensive. Indeed, a claimant should demonstrate, by gathering several indicators, that the relationship is not a commercial one but an employment one. The existence of a single indicator is usually not enough to characterize a relationship of subordination.

*5. Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)* 

Yes, up to 3 years and 5 years for serious undeclared work (_travail dissimulé aggravé_) which is a criminal offense.

*6. Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators* 

The affected driver, the Social Security Authority (URSSAF) and the Labour Inspector.

We do not have evidence of group actions per se, although in Lyon 139 drivers filed individual reclassification claims against Uber before the Labour court. Technically speaking, this is not a class action and the relevant periods of provision of work might differ from driver to driver, but it has similar consequences.

*7. Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?* 



There is no evidence on the impact of a reclassification case on tax and pension allowances, but the driver being reclassified as a platform employee should be able to claim wages, pensions for the relevant period. 

*8. What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?*

The claimant needs to appoint a legal representative and he can apply for legal aid, i.e. help to pay the court and lawyer fees, if eligible.

Justice is relatively accessible and we have been informed that the drivers are helped by an individual advocating for the drivers’ rights and supporting anyone aiming at a reclassification lawsuit against platforms. The individual volunteers to gather all relevant information including personal data to build up the case. 

*9. Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers of the platform in a market at once?* 

A lawsuit brought by the URSSAF or Labour Inspector can bring to a mass reclassification of the whole pool of drivers for a given fiscal year.

Hi [~accountid:6345c2cd5efe6ce125d8176b], 

We just finished the review for Norway. The risk of breach of contract is determined to be high as both Uber and Yango’s ToS prohibit price scraping. Furthermore, criminal liability can be imposed on Bolt and potentially Bolt employees. The risks of criminal liability have been determined to be low/medium but can never be removed. *There is no risk-free way to conduct route fare+ETA window shopping in the RH industry and legal can never green-light such activities.* Please find attached the risk matrix for Norway based on the global approach for price scraping. 

The below process should be followed in Norway in relation to Uber and Yango.

When ToS prohibit data extraction by account holder (which is the case), ability to keep legal risks in check rests on 2 key factors: 

(i) security process and protocol to ensure that activity cannot be easily identified by the target, and

(ii) distancing Bolt from the data collection activity itself and having a legal recourse to a 3rd party service provider.

Basic rule in all cases where target’s ToS prohibits data extraction (which is the case with Uber and Yango) has to be: 

# Engage 3rd party under a dataset acquisition agreement (as opposed to instruction and service agreement) with full indemnifications for Bolt’s benefit under acceptable risk-premium. This is the preferred route but it requires that the 3rd party provider is willing to provide us with full indemnification which could be hard to find. Research on this should be done by the local team to see what the options are [~accountid:5f689921f0d401007029c6b0] 
# If we can’t engage a 3rd party we should do it in-house instead with a focus on security arrangements. The focus should at all times be to keep it small-scale and low-frequency as it is unlikely to cause considerable harm or damage and therefore, such activities would be less vulnerable. However, based on the risk matrix attached this would +require approval from Rides Management+. 

Furthermore, we need to determine which method will be used by the 3rd party provider as we need to confirm that the method ensures both (i) limited scale of the activity; and (ii) better security protocol.

I would also like to highlight that Bolt’s liability would be unlimited in a case of breach of contract.

I suggest you read through this advice and revert with your proposed actions on the window shopping. If we want to use a 3rd party provider we need to initiate discussions with specific vendors in order to determine if they fulfil our requirements on security protocols and indemnification. I suggest you align with your colleagues in Sweden and Finland to find a Nordic approach to this since the advice is more or less the same for all 3 markets in the Nordics. 

Let me know if you have any questions. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

I would only like to add that couriers, at least on the Slovakia market, are able too see roughly, where the order is going to be delivered and how much should they receive for delivering it. Before this system was active, couriers saw the delivery address only, after the order was ready for pick up or they picked it up already. When this was active and the courier didn’t already pick up the order, we were able to change the delivery address without us having to contact the courier and informing him about the change of the delivery address. If the order was already picked up, we would ask the customer, to contact the courier and ask him to deliver the order to the new delivery address. If the courier would agree, we would compensate him of course. 

Now the couriers are able to see roughly, where the order is going to be delivered and how much he is going to receive if the order is delivered. The question is, should we contact the courier, even if he didn’t pick up the order yet about the address change or should we advise the customer to contact the courier immediately? Because if the order was already picked up, we would advise the customer to contact the courier anyway, so couldn’t we ask the eater to contact the courier even, if the order wasn’t picked up yet, but the courier was already assigned?

I am looking forward to your reply!

Hey [~accountid:6345c2cd5efe6ce125d8176b], reviewed the agreement. A few comments from my side:

* The agreement is currently framed as a service agreement (not dataset acquisition agreement) - Bolt instructs Anakin to scrape data from competitors, not that we acquire the dataset of competitor’s data from Anakin.
* Under section 3 Anakin imposes on Bolt all the liabilities arising out of the agreement. This is definitely not acceptable for us under the service agreement.
* Not very clear what the Implementation Fee is in the context of this agreement. Seems to be just an additional fee to the Service Fee for doing the same activities that are agreed between the parties under the agreement (no extra value).
* Under section 7.1 Anakin is entitled to increase the fees agreed between the parties, and we have no grounds to terminate the agreement in such case, but need to wait until the end of the term. The termination of the agreement might occur only in case of material breach of the agreement.
* Under section 9.2 the termination of the agreement seems to be possible only once the Initial Term or a subsequently renewed Term has expired. No possibility to terminate within these Terms.
* Under section 12 Anakin has a very broad clause on the limitation of liability. Basically if the target will claim something from us, we will not be able to claim it back from Anakin. If by any chance we will be able to claim something, then their liability is capped by the ‘FEES PAID BY CUSTOMER TO COMPANY FOR THE SERVICES UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE ONE MONTH PRIOR TO THE ACT THAT GAVE RISE TO THE LIABILITY’.
* Some sections of the T&Cs seem to be skipped - is that an error or are some parts of the T&Cs omitted from the review?



Assuming Anakin will be collecting data from targets whose data is walled off behind Terms & Conditions which prohibit data scraping, the legal risk that might materialise under this agreement is not low. In order for it to be low, we need:

* form the agreement as a dataset acquisition agreement (not service agreement),
* try to negotiate liability waiver for Anakin at least to some extent and impose some liability under a certain premium onto them
* add a clause on full indemnification for Bolt’s benefit (basically amend section 3).

* user invoice generation
* ride-hailing-billing generation
* invoicing fees/app payments generation (only partially affected because of reimport architecture)
* driver earning reports on driverx side (only partially affected, if at all, because of polling; the only drivers affected would be those who did only 0-total rides per day)

Hi [~accountid:5f2cfe232aa2500028d741b9] Please be advised that enabling the feature to just some drivers exposes us to reclassification risk. Please see [this overview |https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xtaUYHVMuARyenb8DOf4DHbyPBVzsraCucAYk4TnC8k/edit]with legal recommendations. 

As a medium risk solution, to mitigate the employment risk and make the feature defensible to some extent, the legal team recommend to structure a Scheduled Rides feature for drivers as an incentive - meaning, if you do X, we enable for you a feature Y:

* *Metrics used for determining whether the incentive applies*. Please note that in order for the risk to be mitigated and the feature to be defensible, the metrics used as X shall not include metrics that measure drivers’ performance *before* the driver has accepted the trip (e.g. acceptance rate). The metrics used as X, however, could include metrics that measure drivers’ performance *after* the driver has accepted the trip (e.g. completed rides, experience of driving on the platform). The metrics for performance measurement after the acceptance of the trip are defensible, since in that case drivers have already committed to the passenger to deliver him/her to the requested destination. If the driver does not honor this commitment, the driver is in breach of the contract concluded between the driver and the rider.

Using the driver score, acceptance rate, completion rate, etc. as a criteria is a high risk option. 

Low risk scenario is enabling to all the drivers. 

I understand that RO RH law requires that RH platforms ensure the high quality of the service, therefore one may claim that only selected (reliable) drivers should be admitted to this feature. Therefore, for the testing phase some selection will be admissible, but ideally in case of positive results of testing phase the feature should be released to all the drivers.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Magda

The main problem with the translation table solution is that it does not scale nicely. Essentially once we launch an experiment, the translation table needs to be maintained indefinitely, so by nature it is not a temporary workaround but rather a technical burden which will need to be addresses ASAP before it becomes an issue. The issue is that we need to come up with a sane cleanup policy so that the db does not become ever growing. It _can_ be done but it will be neither quick nor trivial to implement. At the same time, the transition to a "clean", scalable solution will still be required at some point in the future.
So to recap, the trade-offs:

* Translation table solution - quickest but not scalable. Not acceptable from a technical perspective
* Translation table + cleanup policy - acceptable but not quick
* Clean scalable solution - not quick

At this point I think the implementation cost for solution b is approaching the implementation cost for solution c, so IMHO we should go for c from the get go.

Because of REQ 3 we need to keep track of the original source of a suggestions (google, internal, choose on map, current location etc) in both the delivery-order-history and in the delivery-location subsystems. To illustrate this need, let’s give an example:

Eater selects a delivery location, creates a basket and then, in the checkout screen, moves the pin and confirms the adjusted location as their delivery spot. Next one of two things can happen:

# Eater abandons the order flow and closes the app. At a later stage, eater starts the app anew. The app requests the previous delivery location from BE. At this point, BE needs to know that the delivery location was originally an eater-adjusted pin location in order to not apply the model override
# Eater creates an order. The order details are stored in the deliver-user-order-history subsystem. At a later stage, in a different session, the eater will search for their delivery location via textual search and select this previous order. BE needs to know that this previous order was an eater-adjusted pin location and should not apply the model override.

So both systems that rely on previous orders (real orders or intents to order) should know about the original source of the delivery location.



Because of REQ 5 we need to also keep track of the original coordinates, in case we ever want to send _those_ as opposed to the overridden coordinates.

I would need some help with a new article for the KB and potentially even some training to spread the knowledge for the CS agents.

*context:*

* Fraud recently acquired the ability to decide if we want to keep the preauthorized amount in a Rides order at the time the ride finishes.
* if our decision is to keep the preauth, the remaining amount for the ride will be pushed to the user as debt in their balance. 
* for risky users/payments, we're already live in quite a few countries.

*The issue:*

* Visibility on balance trx history is non-existent. so if the user complains about a surcharge later or why he has a negative balance, CS will struggle to understand where the debt came from.
* I've raise this issue to Balance for them to consider development to improve this visibility, but it might take a while.
* in the meantime, the only solution we can offer is for CS to take a peek on fraud calculation and check if there was a calculation on the checkpoint {{rides_payment_capture_authorized_amount}} which the decision was {{keep_authorized_amount}}. Basically, if there's a debt that isn't visible in trx history and CS needs to dig a bit to find where it comes from, that's how they can currently do it.
** then if there's such decision, they can check the order that matches that date and time to see if it makes sense. essentially, the debt will be the order's final price minus the captured amount which is visible either in the trx history or in the user's payments.
** CS can even potentially skip the check calculation step and try to manually find through the payments if there's a difference to recent orders value, but I'll leave the decision to you on what you think it's the best way for them to find the info.

*Example:* [Order ID|https://westasia-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1330294642], [transaction history|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory?filter=%7B%22filter%22%3A%7B%22source_type%22%3A%22ride_hailing%22%2C%22order_id%22%3A1681211759192086%2C%22target_account_id%22%3A168312677%7D%7D&tz=Atlantic%2FSt_Helena]

* the remaining 3.10 was sent to user's negative balance, but there's no visibility.
* if you check the[ user's calculations|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/userCalculationResults?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22user_id%22%3A168312677%2C%22from%22%3A1678690227.915%7D%7D], you can see the line that shows the decision to keep the authorized amount.

Hey [~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0]! The general answer is that the proposed way of entering into agreements would be valid under Azerbaijani law.

Points to consider:

# We need to stipulate in the form that by filling in the form and accepting the General Terms, the partner accepts not only the terms of the agreement, but also +agrees to making the agreement in the form of electronic document.+  
# Any terms to constitute ‘material terms’ of the agreement must be furnished to the partner, meaning a partner should be allowed an opportunity to download and review the General Terms and we +would need to send the copy of the filled in form+ to the partner together with the General Terms.
# Re the following wording: _Upon acceptance of the General Terms by the Partner and submission of this form to Bolt, the Agreement shall become legally binding unless this Agreement is rejected by Bolt on the following reasons: XYZ?_ - under AZ law, an offer becomes binding on an offeror upon its acceptance by a recipient.  Until then, an offer may be recalled. Otherwise, no recall of accepted offer would be allowed. Therefore, the rejection above would not be valid. However, if the mistake in the details of the partner does not allow to identify such partner, it can be argued that the parties failed to make the agreement in electronic (agreed) form because signing of the agreement by the partner failed. 

Please let me know if you have any further questions on the above.

Here’s how the solution would look like.



We are aiming to replace both the delivery-location subsystem and the delivery-user-order-history subsystem. We will create a new service, {{location-suggestions-delivery-orders}} which will manage both. The storage system we will use for both of the systems will be ElasticSearch. We will maintain two separate indices:

# A {{delivery-order-intent}} index, where each document is an order intent, at most one per user. We will never delete anything from this index, but it will scale with the number of eaters. This will be a direct replacement of the “delivery location” subsystem, meaning that app calls to {{getDeliveryLocation}}  can be served by this subsystem instead of the current one.
# A {{delivery-order}} index, where each document is an order. It will have a clean-up policy of three months (we can extend it to 6 months or more if needed). This will be a direct replacement of the {{order_history_delivery}} table (only for textual suggestion purposes, of course).



As mentioned before, both systems will need to maintain the following metadata:

* Original coordinates (if a model was used to predict these coordinates) - this will allow us to meet REQ 6
* Model metadata (which model version produced the location info) - this will allow us to bulk update/delete/filter bad model prediction, a generalisation of REQ 8
* Original source of the location (textual suggestion, “current location”, “choose on map”) - this will allow us to meet REQ 3
* Current source of the textual suggestion (home, work, delivery_location, rides_history, delivery_history) - for better tracking and analytics
* Place id - for compliance



Thankfully, every location selection (aka order intent) passes through our {{location-suggestions-delivery}} service via the {{recordDeliveryLocationEntered}} endpoint, so we can leverage that. In fact, the existing “delivery location” gets set by LSD precisely on this flow. So in the transition phase, LSD will set the location in both systems (new and old), while providing extra metadata only to the new system.

How do we obtain this metadata? Let’s cover each flow separately

* For textual search results from {{internal}}, {{home}}, {{work}}, {{delivery_location}}, {{rides_history}} and {{delivery_history}} we will suggest overridden coordinates, but also enhance the {{Suggestion}} interface with a new field called {{building_entrance_model_meta}} holding the original lat/lng values and model metadata. When the user selects a suggestion we will receive a {{/recordDeliveryLocationEntered}} call. The request body contains all requested suggestions as they were received from backend. We can identify which suggestion was selected by comparing {{lat}} and {{lng}} fields with the {{lat}} and {{lng}} fields of the request. We can then call {{setDeliveryLocation}} to the new system with metadata: original coordinates & model meta from the {{building_entrance_model_meta}}, “textual search” as the original source, as well as the suggestion place_id.
* For textual search results from {{google}}, we cannot, sadly, do the same thing because these results lack {{lat}} and {{lng}} so there will be nothing for us to override. What we need to do instead is, at {{getPlaceDetails}} time save the required metadata (original coordinates + model meta) inside a Redis. At {{/recordDeliveryLocationEntered}} time we will need to interrogate that Redis and retrieve the metadata.
* For the “current location” and “choose on map at checkout screen” cases, it’s going to be trickier. More on that later, but tl;dr is that we are still going to be using the Redis for that.



Once we store these order intents into our {{delivery-order-intent}} index in {{location-suggestions-delivery-orders}}, every other peace of the puzzle will quickly and neatly fall into place.

Our new {{location-suggesstions-delivery-orders}} service will start subscribing to the {{delivery-order-client-event}} SNS topic. Whenever an order ({{delivered}}, {{failed}}, and {{rejected}}) concludes the service will index a new document into the {{delivery-order}} index. The metadata will be retrieved from the {{delivery-order-intent}} index.

One extra thing to take care of is in {{location-suggestions-delivery}} itself: we will have to now juggle this metadata we get from these two new subsystems and make sure we pass it along in the correct way. For example, if LSD now serves a historical delivery location from LSDO, which it also overrides via the model, it will have to pass the _original coordinates_ (i.e. from LSDO’s response) as suggestion metadata. Same goes for the original source of the location.

Hi [~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0] sharing SK advice - please let me know if you have any questions.



*1. Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied? yes/no* YES

* According to Act No. 125/2006 Coll. on Labour Inspection and on amendment of the Act No. 82/2005 Coll. on Illegal Work and Illegal Employment and on amendment of certain acts state administration in the area of labour inspection shall be performed by state administration bodies, which are the Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Family of the Slovak Republic, the National Labour Inspectorate and Labour Inspectorates.
* The Labor Inspectorate imposes a fine on an employer or a natural person for 1. violation of the violation of the prohibition of illegal employment from 2.000 € to 200.000 € and in the case of illegal employment of two or more natural persons at the same time, at least 5.000 €; 2. performing an activity without an authorization, certificate, license, or permit, if an authorization, certificate, license or permit issued by the National Labor Inspectorate, the labor inspectorate, a natural person or a legal entity according to a special regulation is required to carry out the activity, from 300 € to 33.000 € euros.

*2. Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)* NO

*3. Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria? yes/no* NO

*4. Are reclassification sensitive activity expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?* 

* Any work that fulfills the characteristics of so called dependent work is considered as a work carried out in an employment relationship. 
* Dependent work is work carried out:
*# personally by the employee for the employer within a relationship of employer as superior and employee as subordinate, 
*# in accordance with the employer’s instructions, 
*# in the employer’s name, 
*# during working time determined by the employer. 
* Dependent work shall be carried out solely under employment or a similar labour relationship, or in exceptional cases under different employment arrangements, subject to the conditions set out in the Slovak Labour Code. 
* Dependent work cannot be carried out in a contractual relationship under civil law or commercial law pursuant to special regulations.

*5. Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)* 

* Yes, the statutory limitation period is 3 years, however if claims have been acknowledged in writing, the statutory limitation period is 10 years. 
* A legal entity or a natural person who has been legally fined for violating the prohibition of illegal employment is obliged to pay: 
** a) the agreed wage owed to a natural person who was illegally employed, 
** b) an additional payment in an amount equal to an advance on income tax, income tax, tax arrears on income tax, insurance premium for social insurance according to a special regulation, mandatory contributions for old-age pension savings according to a special regulation, contribution for supplementary pension savings according to a special regulation and the insurance premium for compulsory public health insurance according to a special regulation, which it would be obliged to pay if it properly employed an illegally employed natural person, including relevant sanctions and fines according to special regulations, 
* If not proved otherwise, the agreed wage is the monthly minimum wage according to a special regulation or the wage agreed in a collective agreement for a comparable employee if the collective agreement regulates the wage more favorably than the amount of the monthly minimum wage. 
* If not proved otherwise, it is assumed that the employment relationship lasted three months.

*6. Who is able to take action against Bolt? Couriers / group action / regulators* - Couriers

* Compliance with laws regulating employment relations and working conditions is controlled by the labor inspectorates. Disputes between the employee and the employer regarding the claims from the employment relationships are tried and decided by the courts. 
* If the employer does not meet the employee's claims, the employee has the right to go to the relevant court, which is the only authority to be able to oblige the employer to fulfill the employee's claim, e.g. issuance of the relevant document, payment of wages, severance pay, etc. 
* Neither the labor inspectorate nor the labor inspectors have the ability or competence to take actions on behalf of the employee. The Labor inspectorates do not have the authority to try and decide on employee claims arising from employment relations. Their task is primarily a preventive activity. In order to force the obliged entity to comply with the relevant legal obligation, the labor inspectorates can impose a fine.

*7. Is there any evidence the authorities have considered couriers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?* 

* No evidence that the external counsel is aware of.

*8. What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?*

* There is no need to be represented in the labor law disputes conducted in court. However, an employee can be represented by the attorney at law or the trade union as well. If an employee is not represented by the attorney at law or the trade union, a special so called manuduction duty of the court is established, which is constructed more broadly than the court's general information obligation. Its purpose is balancing the procedural inequality of the disputing parties. 
* In general, the range of fees is 6% of the value of the subject matter (min 16,50 €/ max 16.596,50 €) if the value of the subject matter can be calculated or if the value of the subject matter cannot be assessed a fee is stated at 99.,50 €. But the plaintiff is not subject to the court fee, if it is an individual labor dispute and the plaintiff is not an employer

*9. Can claims be made to reclassify all couriers of the platform in a market at once?*

* No, the Labor Inspectorates/courts try and decide cases individually. 
* There is a possibility that all couriers/drivers will be included in one decision of the Labor Inspectorate, but at the same time this must be preceded by a review of the contractual relations of all couriers and drivers by the Labor Inspectorate. It is highly unlikely.

Hello [~accountid:5ff6fd9c64208901410c741c], good morning.

Before closing this ticket (unless you need to discuss anything else), I noticed that you also asked this question: _“How do you distinguish between 0% VAT and out of scope, for example, or between VAT exempt and out of scope?”_

For tax purposes (in general and broad terms) *_“Out of scope”_* means that a transaction *is completely disregarded for tax purposes*. It is as if such a transaction _“does not exist and never happened”_ for tax purposes, which means that the person who carried out such a transaction does not have to pay any tax due and, additionally, does not have to comply with any formal obligations related to such transaction (declaration or reporting to the tax authorities).

For instance, public fines that are meant to be passed through to the users. Such a transaction falls out of the scope of VAT, so we don’t have to charge VAT to the user (thus, we don’t have to settle any VAT tax due arising from such pass-through) and, additionally, we don’t have to provide the user with an invoice (regardless of the statement that we will produce to inform the user about the fine being passed through). This means that we don’t have to declare such a transaction in any VAT return (not even for informative purposes).

For VAT purposes, *0% rated is equivalent to exempt*. Once again in broad terms, it means that the taxpayer does not have to settle any tax due (because the tax due is zero, as the tax rate is 0%), but the taxpayer does have to comply with formal obligations and include the transaction in the relevant returns for information purposes.

For instance, an exportation of goods from the EU to countries outside the EU qualify as zero-rated transactions (exempted transactions), so the taxpayer does not have to settle a VAT tax due, but the taxpayer is subject to VAT and customs clearance compliance obligations, which means that the tax authorities must be informed about such a transaction, although no tax due was collected.

I hope this clarifies this topic. Should you require further guidance, please let me know.

Hi Julia, these are the responses for CY: 

*Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied? yes/no?*

Yes

*Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc.)*

No.

From previous communication we had with the Department of Road Transport of the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Works (the “*Department of Road Transport*”), we understand that even though various complaints regarding non-compliance by taxi drivers operating via a platform were raised to the authorities which were subsequently reported to the Cypriot police and the Law Office of the Republic of Cyprus by the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Works (the “*Licensing Authority*”), there are currently no court decisions relating to such complaints.

We are neither aware of any litigation against platforms in Cyprus (noting that there is no publicly available litigation register in Cyprus).

 *Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria? yes/no*

The criteria for determining whether an individual is an employee or independent contractor are not specified in legislation and these have developed via case law. 

In Cyprus, according to case law, determination of whether a person is an independent contractor or employee, is a matter to be determined by the Courts. In determining such relationship and whether an independent contractor is an employee, the Court will take into account, inter alia, the following factors: 

(a)     the parties’ intention when establishing the relationship;

(b)     the degree of integration of such person in the business;

(c)      the degree of control exercised by the client against such person;

(d)     the degree of financial risk assumed by such person (the “independent contractor”);

(e)     whether such person use his/her own equipment (e.g. vehicle) or that of the client;

(f)       the independence of such person when exercising his services;

(g)     the economic realities of the relationship such as whether or not emoluments depend on performance as well as the opportunity for profit from the performance of the tasks of such person;

(h)     the responsibility for payment of social insurance contributions and income tax; and

(i)       any other relevant factor.

*Are reclassification sensitive activity expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?*

 No. See our reply to question no 3 above.

*Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)*

Yes. Please note that claims may also be made for unpaid contributions.

*Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators*

Determination of the status of a person (i.e. whether such person is an independent contractor or employee) is usually sought following the termination of the relationship with such person. Drivers may also during their employment bring an action (in which several drivers may join as joint-plaintiffs or authorise one party to represent them in such action) for reclassification of their status from independent contractors to employees and/or a declaratory order as to their status. 

Additionally, although not directly related to reclassification, the Department of Road Transport and the Licensing Authority have jurisdiction over the road transport area and can refer a potential breach by Bolt to the Law Office of the Republic of Cyprus. If the Law Office of the Republic of Cyprus believes that there is a case against Bolt, it may initiate court proceedings against Bolt (e.g. pursuant to section 21 of the Law on the Regulation of Traffic Transport of 1982 (as amended), which provides that any person who uses a motor vehicle or causes, allows or tolerates the use of such vehicle in contravention of this law, or any of the regulations issued pursuant to this law, can be found criminally liable and subject to imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months and/or to a fine not exceeding EUR 768).

*Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?*

No, as far as we are aware.

*What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?*

Legal representation by an advocate is not always mandatory before the Courts in the Republic of Cyprus for persons of sound mind and of legal age, but it is highly recommended for more complex cases. 

Filing fees and other court-related expenses vary depending on the type of case, the court involved and the amount of the claim. Court fees and lawyer fees based on court scales are relatively low in Cyprus and do not constitute a significant obstacle in the access to justice.

The official languages in the Republic of Cyprus are Greek and Turkish. While English is widely spoken, court proceedings and legal documents are generally in Greek. This may create a language barrier for some individuals seeking access to justice.

Resolution of civil disputes before the Courts is currently severely delayed due to a backlog of cases before the civil courts in Cyprus and claims usually take 5-7 years be determined.

*Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers of the platform in a market at once?*

The concept of a class/group action does not exist in Cyprus. However, if a number of individuals (e.g. drivers) wanted their status to be reclassified (i.e. from independent contractors to employees), they would be able to either initiate an action together and/or authorize one party to represent them in such action.

 Please let me know if you have any follow up questions? 

Best, 

Liisa

script

{code:sql}with qr_code_change_ts as (
  select vehicle_id, created qr_code_change_ts
  from ng_rental.rental_fleet_vehicle_change_log
 where type = 'uuid'
 and created_date >=date'2023-02-01'
 ),
 log as (
select e.id, e.created,e.vehicle_id,e.from_state ,e.to_state, qrc.qr_code_change_ts
from ng_rental.rental_order_vehicle_state_event e
join qr_code_change_ts qrc 
	on qrc.vehicle_id=e.vehicle_id 
where e.created_date >=date'2023-02-01'
and e.type='state'
and (
	(e.from_state in ('lost','operational') and e.to_state = 'collected') 
	or 
	(e.from_state='being_serviced' and e.to_state = 'collected')
	)
order by e.vehicle_id  asc, e.id, e.created asc
)
select date_trunc('week',qr_code_change_ts),count(distinct vehicle_id),1.0*avg(time_till_next_event)/60
from (
select *,
lead(from_state,1) over (partition by vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by created asc, id asc) next_from_state,
lead(to_state,1) over (partition by vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by created asc, id asc) next_to_state,
lead(created,1) over (partition by vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by created asc, id asc) next_created,
case when qr_code_change_ts between created and lead(created,1) over (partition by vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by created asc, id asc) then 1 else 0 end qr_code_change_happened,
date_diff('minute',created,lead(created,1) over (partition by vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by created asc, id asc)) time_till_next_event
from log
order by vehicle_id  asc, id asc , created asc
)
where 
	from_state in ('lost','operational') 
	and to_state='collected' 
	and next_from_state='being_serviced' 
	and next_to_state='collected'
	and qr_code_change_happened=1
group by 1
order by 1 asc
{code}

# find out all qr code changes in {{qr_code_change_ts}}
# find out events happening with scooters with qr code changes. We’re interested in: collections from lost/operational (aka ‘collect for service’), and collections from being_serviced (aka end service)
# if there’s a set of events: ‘collected for service' and ‘end service’ from 2) and there’s a QR code change between them -then we’re interested in that
# we measure avg time between two events, hoping that it will decrease

Hi  [~accountid:63a583d78a07cbd184a96e54] thanks for reaching out. The proposed wording to implement Service Fee, approved by our tax, is as follows (to be added to section 6.2 of [the Bolt Food t&c|https://static.food.bolt.eu/legalDocument/nrgLDkP3kVFxmeJD1XlQx/V5%20of%20Bolt-Client%20T%26C%20(PL)%20-PL-.pdf]):

* *_The Courier Fee may include service fees in order to cover the cost of promotion investments._*
* Proposed PL wording: *_Opłata Kurierska może zawierać opłatę serwisową pobieraną w celu pokrycia kosztów promocyjnych._*   

As PL market is a consumer-sensitive market (and also PL consumer protection is very strict on the clarity of consumer fees, the way of presenting them and possibilities to avoid them, e.g. cases: [OLX|https://uokik.gov.pl/news.php?news_id=18892], [Vinted|https://uokik.gov.pl/news.php?news_id=18517], [Ebilet/Eventim/Ticketmaster|https://uokik.gov.pl/news.php?news_id=19416]; but also [Glovo/Uber Eats|https://uokik.gov.pl/news.php?news_id=17945]), I did some brief research how the competitors regulate service fee in their t&c, e.g.:

# Glovo - service fee [section 6|https://glovoapp.com/en/legal/terms/]: ”_Glovo will charge the User a service fee for the use of our Platform in order to continuously improve our overall services, providing a wider selection of vendors and continuously improving our user experience, among others._ 
_The amount of the service fee can be fixed or variable according to the value of the products. Glovo sets the service and makes it visible to Users at the moment of the checkout of every order._ 
_This service fee will be charged against the credit card that you have selected for the payment of the order. In the event that you have selected the cash payment option (this option may be unavailable in some of the countries in which Glovo operates), the service fee will be charged to you in cash at the time of collection or delivery of your order, and the store will be responsible for receiving this amount on behalf of and in the name of Glovo.”_
# Wolt - service fee [pkt. 3|https://explore.wolt.com/pl/pol/terms]: “Partners or Wolt will charge Users a delivery fee and a service fee.“


For the testing phase - the wording approved by our tax team should be sufficient. However, we might need to revisit it once the testing is done and you have full clarity of how the fee is calculated, structured and used.

As all consumer t&c changes in PL must be announced in advance of its implementation (so that the user have time to analyse, be aware, etc.), an advance 10-14 days notice will required, therefore in practice the change will go live end of April/ 1 May. Will keep you posted. 

Please let me know if you have any questions or comments. thanks!

Magda

I’ll try to document here what happened, in case we get it again:

# Our default English translations don’t have any backslashes, and it’s correct, that’s how it should be.
# Crowdin automatically proposes to escape double quotes. I’m not entirely sure why it does that, but for now that’s OK (we don’t have many cases of complex html being added to translations). If we get more cases like this, maybe we should do something about it.
# Because of these warnings, it seems that some translators accepted the proposed changes. The warning looks like this:
!image-20230414-110621.png|width=600,height=229!

# Because of that, translations were saved with {{\"}} instead of just {{"}}.
# Later, developers started looking at responses from the backend, and noticed that the double quotes appear like this: {{\\\"}}. This is when we got alerted.
# However, there is actually no problem. JS string like {{"foo \\\" bar"}} is actually just {{foo \" bar}}, it just needs to escape both characters in order to make this string valid json or js code.
# Some devs appeared to be very confused about this (which is understandable), and kept asking why our backend does double escaping. However, it’s just a representational issue, the backend is actually responding with the string exactly as it is defined in Crowdin.
# In the end, I just did this:
## explained that the backend truly responds with whatever we have in Crowdin
## got crowdin proofreader access and tweaked all strings not to have {{\}} at all
# With that, I consider this ticket to be done. If we get more cases like this in the future, we can investigate more (e.g. change crowdin settings if possible to disable this warning). For now, however, everything is fine, and I guess that translators will keep their strings consistent by themselves.

# Clause 4.14 - we have 2000 UAH because in the Global version of the Driver T&Cs the amount for such damage is 50 EUR, with 2000 UAH being the rough equivalent. According to clause 4.7 of [+Passenger T&Cs+|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/ua/new-terms-for-riders/], if the passenger does not pay the penalty and/or compensate the damage, Bolt may pursue the claims on behalf of the provider of the transport service. Generally our actions and the recovery of this amount would depend on the circumstances of a particular case. We also might choose to compensate the driver for the damage using our own funds.
# We don’t have restrictions about the age of the passenger because we are not verifying the age of the passenger in the app. Since we don’t do that, we cannot really put this in the T&Cs until we really have mechanism to control whether there is an adult or minor ordering the ride. However, in our self-help page we have that information because the laws of Ukraine have such restrictions, but again we cannot control that, and the driver has to comply with the laws regulating the provision of the transportation services. In clause 2.1.3 of the Driver T&Cs we also put the following obligation on the driver: “_all the information and documents you have presented to us (including the Driver’s documents and the documents on his vehicle and other conditions necessary for certain Bolt categories,_ +_such as child seat,_+ _etc.) are accurate, correct, complete and up to date_“.

{code:sql}WITH duplicates AS (
-- For duplicates (is in declined_driver_registration_log_id): For each lead ID identify the last recorded lead ID that followed
-- Then based on the last recorded lead ID identify the first recorded lead ID as the Master Lead ID
-- NB! We previously used a Recursive Query in Redshift for this but this Recursive Queries are not supported by Presto
-- Now a huge number of left joins have to do the job. The 20 joins covers 99.5% of duplicates
SELECT
    sd_1.declined_driver_registration_log_id AS lead_id,
    GREATEST(
    COALESCE(sd_1.new_driver_registration_log_id,0),
    COALESCE(sd_2.new_driver_registration_log_id,0),
    COALESCE(sd_3.new_driver_registration_log_id,0),
    COALESCE(sd_4.new_driver_registration_log_id,0),
	COALESCE(sd_5.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_6.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_7.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_8.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_9.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_10.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_11.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_12.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_13.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_14.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_15.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_16.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_17.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_18.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_19.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0),
	COALESCE(sd_20.new_driver_registration_log_id, 0)
    ) AS last_lead_id
FROM
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_1
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_2
    ON sd_1.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_2.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_3
    ON sd_2.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_3.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_4
    ON sd_3.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_4.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_5
    ON sd_4.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_5.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_6
    ON sd_5.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_6.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_7
    ON sd_6.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_7.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_8
    ON sd_7.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_8.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_9
    ON sd_8.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_9.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_10
    ON sd_9.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_10.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_11
    ON sd_10.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_11.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_12
    ON sd_11.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_12.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_13
    ON sd_12.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_13.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_14
    ON sd_13.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_14.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_15
    ON sd_14.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_15.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_16
    ON sd_15.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_16.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_17
    ON sd_16.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_17.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_18
    ON sd_17.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_18.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_19
    ON sd_18.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_19.declined_driver_registration_log_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.driver_registration_driver_registration_log_silently_declined AS sd_20
    ON sd_19.new_driver_registration_log_id = sd_20.declined_driver_registration_log_id
),
duplicates_with_last_new_lead_id AS (
-- Appends the last new lead_id to the chain
SELECT * FROM duplicates
UNION ALL
SELECT last_lead_id AS id, last_lead_id
FROM duplicates GROUP BY 1,2
),
master_lead_raw AS (
-- Get first recorded lead id based on duplicates that have the same last recorded lead id
SELECT
    lead_id,
    last_lead_id,
    MIN(lead_id) OVER (PARTITION BY last_lead_id) AS master_lead_id
FROM
    duplicates_with_last_new_lead_id
),
master_lead AS (
-- cleaned version to remove duplicate lead IDs
SELECT
    lead_id,
    MIN(master_lead_id) AS master_lead_id
FROM
    master_lead_raw
GROUP BY
    lead_id
),
master_lead_chains AS (
--Append leads with no duplication chains (lead_id not in fleet_driver_registration_log.id)
SELECT
    master_lead_id,
    lead_id
FROM
    master_lead
UNION ALL
SELECT
    fdrl.id AS master_lead_id, -- for lead_ids that have no duplicates, the master_lead_id will the be the same as the lead id
    fdrl.id AS lead_id
FROM
    ng_public.fleet_driver_registration_log AS fdrl
LEFT JOIN
    master_lead AS ml
    ON ml.lead_id = fdrl.id
WHERE
    ml.lead_id IS NULL
),
raw_base AS (
-- Create raw base with master_lead_id, lead_id and driver and partner information under lead_id
-- This only associates driver_id with the succesfully registered lead_id
SELECT
    mlc.master_lead_id,
    mlc.lead_id,
    fd.id AS driver_id,
    master_fdrl.created AS master_lead_created,
    fdrl.created AS lead_created,
    fd.created AS driver_created,
    fd.status AS driver_status,
    fdrl.status AS lead_status,
    fd.company_id,
    fd.driver_root_id AS partner_id,
    fdrl.email,
    fdrl.first_name,
    fdrl.last_name,
    fdrl.username,
    fdrl.phone,
    fdrl.personal_code,
    fdrl.driver_license 
FROM
    master_lead_chains AS mlc
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.fleet_driver_registration_log AS fdrl
    ON fdrl.id = mlc.lead_id
LEFT JOIN
    ng_public.fleet_driver_registration_log AS master_fdrl
    ON master_fdrl.id = mlc.master_lead_id
LEFT JOIN
	ng_public.fleet_driver AS fd
    ON fdrl.driver_id = fd.id)
SELECT 
master_lead_id,
lead_id,
master_lead_created,
lead_created,
date(lead_created) AS lead_created_date, -- for partitioning
driver_created,
partner_id,
-- For each master_lead_id, broadcast the latest available drive/partner_id to earlier lead_ids with null driver/partner_id
last_value(driver_id) IGNORE NULLS OVER (PARTITION BY master_lead_id ORDER BY lead_created DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS driver_id_full, 
last_value(partner_id) IGNORE NULLS OVER (PARTITION BY master_lead_id ORDER BY lead_created DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS partner_id_full,
current_timestamp AS _last_ingested
FROM raw_base{code}

*BELGIUM*

# *Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied?*  Yes, as of 1 January 2023. 



*2. Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)* Yes. The Belgian labour inspection services have published an action plan for 2023-2034 in which they have announced that they will target, among others:

 

* *the platform economy* – At least 10 joint investigations will be carried out by the labour and social security authorities in the platform economy.

  

* *the taxi sector* (both online platforms and the so-called "classic" are targeted). It is announced that at least 10 controls will be carried out in the "car rental with driver" sector (control of social legislation), with a view to the focus on self-employed persons working for platforms in the broad sense of the term.

 *3. Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria?*   

Yes, it is. The so-called “Labour Deal” in force as of 1 January 2023 introduced a rebuttable presumption of the existence of an employment contract, based on specific criteria for the platform economy. If at least 3 of the 8 legal criteria or 2 of the last 5 criteria are fulfilled, there is a presumption of the existence of an employment contract. This presumption can be rebutted by all means of law.

*4. Are reclassification sensitive activity expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?*

Any activity that will fall under the meaning of the below 8 criteria 



|1° the possibility of exclusivity|By this is meant, for example, a platform that in any way prohibits or restricts the worker to work and/or cooperate with another principal or employer operating in the same sector.|
|2° the possibility of using geolocation for other purposes than the proper functioning of its basic
services|A platform can, for example, use geolocation to identify workers participating in a demonstration.|
|3° the possibility of restricting the free choice of ways of working|This applies, for example, to the drivers who cannot freely choose the route.|
|4° the possibility to limit the income level of a platform worker|An example of this is a platform using an algorithm to reduce or limit the number or type of journeys a worker can make.|
|5° the possibility to enforce rules of appearance, behaviour and performance of work|For example, it involves a platform that imposes dress codes on drivers or requires them to wear certain accessories( uniform ). Obviously, this does not involve, for example, compliance with traffic rules.|
|6° the possibility to have the prioritisation of future work offers, the amount bid for a job and/or determination of ranking determined by evaluating the past work performance of the platform worker|This criterion applies, for example, to a platform that imposes a certain level of performance and that sanctions a worker who fails to achieve this level.|
|7° the possibility of restriction of the freedom of the work organisation|This applies, for example, to platforms that reward or sanction a worker according to the working time or the time that he is logged in to the services.|
|8° the possibility of restricting building up a customer base or to work for third parties|In doing so, the aim is, for example, to prevent the worker from contacting a client outside the platform for whom he performed a service.|

*5. Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)* 

*Employee's claims for salary arrears etc.)* – Under Belgian labour law, an employee can claim for the payment of salary (+*end-of-year bonus, holiday, extra time, indemnity in lieu of notice) up* to +*five years*+ in arrears provided that (s)he has filed a claim based on the contract of employment +*within one year of its termination*+. 

However, as default in paying due salary to an employee is deemed a "+*continued offence*+", the misclassified employee can actually claim +*for more than five years in arrears*+. Indeed, the said employee can actually claim for arrears since the first default of payment started. In a case of employee misclassification, it means that the employee can claim for salary arrears for the entire period of employment.

*Social security's claims for contributions* – Vis-à-vis the National Social Security Office ("NSSO"), the statutes of limitations are of +three years, or seven years in case of fraud+ for the payment of the company's social security contributions (+/- 27%) and the employee's contribution (13,07%) (both to be supported by the employer). This being said, in case of successful claim by the driver, social security charges will have to be paid on all payments of arrears due (if the case arises, +*from the start of his/her occupation*+ following the reclassification of self-employment as an employment contract).

*6. Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators* 

Drivers (individually) before the Labour court or before the Administrative Commission which can issue  non-binding advice on the nature of a particular labour relationship and the NSSO (regulator).

In Belgium, the class action is limited to a certain number of specific cases (mainly consumer law) and would not apply in case of reclassification claim. But in practice, (i) several workers can jump into the reclassification proceedings initiated by one or more workers, or (ii) the labour authorities can summon a platform operator in order to claim the reclassification of (part of) its personnel.   



*7. Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?* 

The law has been recently entered into force and there’s no case law so far based on the new law.

Notwithstanding, in principle, self-employed drivers are not entitled to employment benefits from the platform operator. However, the Labour Deal provides the new obligation for platform operators to take out an accident insurance for their self-employed platform workers.  This obligations is not yet applicable: its entry into force depends on the publication of a decree which has not yet been published.

*8*. *What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?*

In the event of a lawsuit brought before the Labour court, the parties have to appoint a lawyer. However, the new law introduced the possibility to ask for a non-binding advice issued by the Administrative Commission. This procedure is cheap, simple and fast. It is a very low-threshold procedure. Also, the driver does not necessarily have to hire a lawyer. It can also be seen as a first ‘test’ to see the chance of success before eventually going to court. If the driver receives a positive decision, it may have a precedential value. The decision can be directive for the court.

# *Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers of the platform in a market at once?*
