Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] 

Here is a response from our external advisor in Hungary.

*1. Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied? yes/no*

 Yes.

In Hungary, companies often conclude service contracts instead of employment agreement for the performance of certain tasks. Such service contracts are usually entered into with individuals or with companies established by individuals, who will perform the services for the benefit of the company.

The usual purpose of concluding service contracts instead of employment agreements is that

* it results in a much more favourable tax burden for the employer compared to paying a salary under an employment relationship and
* the employer does not need to apply certain stringent provisions of the Labour Code (LC) such as those on working time, rest periods and the paid annual leave,
* the termination procedure for service contracts is significantly simpler than that for an employment.

The relevant practice of Hungarian authorities and courts regarding classification of service contracts has extensively developed in recent years, as a result of which some distinguishing characteristics between service contracts and employment agreements have been established. The case law on the tax treatment of such reclassifications has developed as well.

In light of the above, it is important to distinguish between service contracts and employment relationships and put the appropriate contract in place, in respect of each individual performing work for the company in order to mitigate potential reclassification risks.

If a service contract is reclassified as an employment agreement, following potential consequences/sanctions may apply:

* the Labour Authority may impose a fine of HUF 30,000 – HUF 10,000,000 on the company concerned depending on the number of employees and violations, and the seriousness of these
* the Tax Authority may impose negative consequences, such as
** the personal income taxes, social security and other contributions not paid by the employer due to the use of service contract must be paid retroactively together with tax penalties and late charges
** further, the VAT charged by the party to the other contracting party must be revised as well, since the service provided in the framework of an employment is not subject to VAT.
* potential individual employee claims of drivers cannot be excluded within a general 3-years limitation period. Such claims usually arise when the contract relationship terminates.

*2. Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc.)?*

There is no specific focus on platforms in respect of reclassification. On the other hand, all sectors and all market players may be subject to inspection anytime, both from labour and from tax perspective.

 

*3. Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria? yes/no*

Yes.

Usually service contracts take the form of either agency contract ("megbízási szerződés") or a contract for work ("vállalkozási szerződés"), both regulated by the Hungarian Civil Code.

The distinction between a contract for work and an employment relationship is rather clear. In the contract for work relationship the contractor undertakes to provide a work product agreed.

The distinction between the employment relationship and the agency relationship is, however, not so clear. The assignment under an agency contract qualifies as a "transaction or management of affairs" since the agent is obliged to administer the matter assigned to him in line with the instructions and with due consideration of the interests of the principal. Accordingly, the agent must act on behalf of and in the interests of the principal but he/she does not necessarily provide a specific result.

As it was ruled on several occasions by the Hungarian courts, it is the substance of the agreement and never the form or name of the agreement given by the parties that is decisive. Pursuant to the Hungarian Civil Code, a fictional contract is null and void and if such contract is intended to disguise another contract, the relationship of the parties is to be judged on the basis of the disguised contract (reclassification).

There is no particular definition of the employment relationship in the LC. Labour courts, however, characterise the legal relationship based on several elements. Primary and secondary characteristics may determine whether an agreement is an employment agreement or a service contract.

Primary Characteristics are determinative, the existence of any such characteristics in an agreement may indicate the existence of an employment agreement.

* The main characteristic of the employment relationship is the job profile. If the contract defines the actual work duties to be performed regularly similarly as a "job profile", this may establish the existence of an employment relationship.
* The tasks shall be performed personally. Under an employment agreement, an employee may not use a subcontractor or his own employee for the work.
* The obligation of employment. Under the employment agreement, the employee shall be provided work by the employer, and the employee shall be available to the employer.
* Subordination. The employer has the rights of an employer under the Labour Code and has control and instruction rights. If the wording of the contract provides that the job profile or the scope of activities requires continuous supervision and a close organizational link between the parties, this may also be a feature of an employment contract. This legal dependence is an obvious mark of an employment agreement.

Secondary Characteristics have no decisive factor but may assist to define the type of legal relationship.

* Extensive right of the employer to instruct the employee. The principle of the right to instruct was manifested in court judgments as follows. The court found that if an individual or the company established by him has to report to the other contracting party in relation to his work, this moves their relationship towards being characterized as an employment relationship. If a party may control or supervise the other's work during or related to any phase, any detail of the work, it is likely to be an employment relationship.
* The time of work is also an important issue. The performance of work on a regular, continuous basis is a feature of employment contracts (i.e. the party is obliged to appear regularly – every day – at the company’s premises or attend regular meetings or consultations). In addition, if the relevant contract contains provisions regarding the time framework or if the employee is obliged to record his working hours, this may also support such a qualification. The annual leave paid by the employer further strengthens the relationship being characterized as an employment relationship. The real question is, who has the right to dispose of over working hours. If not the party carrying out the tasks, it may be an employment relationship, however, certain types of work (e-working) do not adhere to this rule. The quantity of working hours is not a decisive factor, either.
* The place of work is also an important feature. If the place of work is specified in the contract this represents an element of an employment relationship, since the place of work is generally not specified by the parties in an agency agreement. However, the mere fact that the contracted person performs work at the premises of the company does not necessarily mean that the relationship between the parties is an employment relationship.
* The remuneration for the work is also a typical distinguishing characteristic. It is irrelevant if the remuneration is defined as an agency or other fee where such remuneration qualifies as a personal salary according to its nature. If the fees are payable on a monthly basis, on a definite day of each month in a fixed amount, the relationship is likely to qualify as an employment relationship.
* The contracting party’s use of the company’s infrastructure, office premises, computers, telephone, etc. – also suggests the existence of an employment relationship. The contracting fee may consist expressly of the costs of the performance incurred by the "employee". The legal relationship may also be classified as an employment relationship if the company pays a daily allowance or disbursement to the "employee" in a contractual relationship with the company for the days of business travel in the country or abroad. A further important issue is whether the individual uses his own equipment or the equipment of the employer.

It should also be noted that the daily routine of parties’ cooperation is important as well. It is not enough to define the terms smartly in the contract but also the actual day-to-day routine must conform to the above-mentioned criteria in order to avoid reclassification.

 

*4. Are reclassification-sensitive activities expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?*

All sectors/activities/all market players may be subject to inspection anytime, both from labour and tax perspective.

On the basis of primary and secondary characteristics, (labour and tax) authorities, as well as courts, have the competence to imply an employment relationship and draw consequences on the basis of such reclassification.

 

*5. Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings)?*

Yes. In case of reclassification, claims can be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings).

Both labour and tax authorities are entitled to classify contract relationships on the basis of their content and characteristics. The potential result of reclassification is that direct employment can be established by the authorities and legal consequences would be drawn on the basis of such supposed direct employment. This means that:

(i)     labour authorities may apply sanctions (labour fine within the range of HUF 30,000 and 10,000,000 (app. EUR 75 - 25,000)) due to disregarding restrictions of the Labour Code,

(ii)    tax authorities may establish non-compliance with tax laws and tax deficits which may potentially affect all tax types (corporate, VAT and income tax) as well as social security contributions. Such tax deficiencies may be established for the entire limitation period of 5 years, and

(iii)   potential individual employee claims of drivers cannot be excluded within a general 3-years limitation period.

 

*6. Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers (Couriers) / group action / regulators?*

Reclassification initiatives are usually raised by authorities, either labour or tax authorities.

Also, contractors (drivers) can initiate a claim for establishing their employee status/entitlement to certain benefits arising from / based on the employment relationship. This is usually raised when the contractual relationship terminates.

Group action does not exist in practice.

 

*7. Is there any evidence that the authorities have considered Drivers (Couriers) eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities, etc)?*

No specific decision for similar platforms.

However, there is constant scrutiny on all sectors/activities in this respect, and from time to time labour and/or tax authorities focus on specific sectors/activities/market players, etc.

 

*8. What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, the requirement to have a representative, etc.)?*

This question is relevant for individual claims of contractors (drivers). Their access to justice is relatively easy, if they claim to be treated as employees they will be released from payment of court fees in advance. Only if they lose the claim will they have to pay (reduced) court fees.

There is no specific administrative issue hindering such relatively easy access to justice.

 

*9. Can claims be made to reclassify all Drivers (Couriers) of the platform in a market at once?*

If labour or tax authorities start an investigation that results in reclassification, that may affect all / several drivers at once.

If one of the drivers initiates a claim for being treated as an employee, the case will be limited to his/her specific case only. (In such case this may, however, serve as a reason for other drivers too to set a claim for such benefits / initiate litigation against the company.)

*Option 1:* Making an application to set aside the judgment (which is the option outlined below) however as you mentioned this comes at a cost, I appreciate that the cost per application means that it is more costly than the 3 judgments itself. 

*Option 2:* If the debt is paid to the claimant within one month of the CCJ - If the debt is paid in full within 1 month of the date of the CCJ, you can apply to the court to have the entry in the Register removed. You need to get a certificate from the court to prove you've paid off the debt. There is a fee to pay for the certificate.  If the entry is removed from the Register, the credit reference agencies will be told and details of your CCJ will be removed from your record.

Unfortunately, due to the lapse of time we cannot use option 2. This default judgment was issued in October 2022.

Hi, Polina! I received the following re AZ:

# We need to stipulate in the form that by filling in the form and accepting the General Terms, the partner accepts not only the terms of the agreement, but also +agrees to making the agreement in the form of electronic document.+  
# Any terms to constitute ‘material terms’ of the agreement must be furnished to the partner, meaning a partner should be allowed an opportunity to download and review the General Terms and we +would need to send the copy of the filled in form+ to the partner together with the General Terms.
# Re the following wording: _Upon acceptance of the General Terms by the Partner and submission of this form to Bolt, the Agreement shall become legally binding unless this Agreement is rejected by Bolt on the following reasons: XYZ?_ - under AZ law, an offer becomes binding on an offeror upon its acceptance by a recipient.  Until then, an offer may be recalled. Otherwise, no recall of accepted offer would be allowed. Therefore, the rejection above would not be valid. However, if the mistake in the details of the partner does not allow to identify such partner, it can be argued that the parties failed to make the agreement in electronic (agreed) form because signing of the agreement by the partner failed. 

Based on the above, I suggest adding something like this:

_Upon acceptance of the General Terms by the Partner and submission of this form to Bolt, the Agreement shall become legally binding unless the Agreement is not deemed concluded as determined by Bolt in its own sole discretion (including but not limited to due to missing or invalid data)._ *_The Partner acknowledges that the Agreement is made in the form of electronic document._*

The last part in bold should be added to AZ form, not needed GH, NG and PT.

Actually, page is working correctly-ish.

Information there comes from 3 places:

# Packages (i.e. application configs) from Builder DB
# CDS service infos while filtering by service group (equivalent of package)
# Load CODEOWNERS from local git repo and get owner by matching CDS service info bootstrap path

Meanwhile, service ownership information was added to CDS, so step 3 can be skipped since the service codeowner comes in step 2.

However, since the information comes from 2 sources, it’s difficult to implement server side pagination and filtering.

Options:

# Send all data to client and do client-side pagination and filtering
# Build a server-side cache with all the data, refresh it from a cron
# Add ownership information to package - create a new column in application config, use a cron to read service ownership info for package from CDS, update the table
# Do nothing (and possibly remove filtering by codeowner to fix UX)

Concerns:

* Option 1 - scales with the number of page loads, can be heavy on the CDS side since we’re moving around all the service metadata
* Option 2 has the downside that cluster mapping information needs to be fresh, because it’s updated from the same page. We can get around this by loading the mapping info from DB on each request → load package info from cache, load package mapping info from DB, merge results
* Option 3 - no implementation concerns here. The question is if we want to keep the link between packages and service ownership at this level strategically
* Option 4 - cheapest, but it hides the problem

h2. Investigation Outcome

The payments routed to the Adyen cards can be segregated into three different categories based on the payment's business line: subscriptions, business, and others.

*Subscriptions:* There are two ways to route these payments to the Processout cards.

# Ask the teams managing these subscriptions to point to the Processout cards instead of the Adyen cards.
# Since these payments are small in number, we can also delete the Adyen cards and ask users to resubscribe. When users resubscribe, these subscriptions will automatically point to the Processout cards.

*Business:* Ask the teams managing these subscriptions to point to the Processout cards instead of the Adyen cards.

*Others:* This includes all other business lines. For these, we have observed that the expiry date of the cards stored in the Processout is in the past, even if the actual expiry date is in the future. So the Processout cards are marked as expired in our system while the corresponding Adyen cards are marked as active. As a result, the Adyen cards are prioritized over the Processout cards. There are two ways to solve this:

# Ask Processout to correct the expiry date of the cards stored in their system. After that, update the expiry date of the corresponding cards in our database.
# Set the expiry date of the corresponding Adyen cards in the past. This would force users to re-add those cards, and newly added cards would be stored in Processout.

One potential use case would be team notification & the todo list for each team. This is more about team’s dashboard rather than service’s, but [~accountid:60a8d308c8c05a0069800b2a] asked me to post here, so here I go 😄 

There are multiple use cases where we need to notify the team to do something, and then keep reminding the team about it just in case, so that they wouldn’t forget it. Existing use cases are:

# disabled tests & pending PRs disabling failing tests – as soon as team’s test fails in develop or master, we notify them with a Slack message and open a PR, and then every week we ping them in Slack about the list of pending PRs and disabled tests (which are otherwise dead code and are very easy to forget about)
# dynamic config approvals – once request is created, we will need to notify about the request, and also potentially keep track of such requests and keep reminding to handle them (suggestion from here: [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C03UY0T0WV7/p1681221108014459?thread_ts=1681136821.761299&cid=C03UY0T0WV7|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C03UY0T0WV7/p1681221108014459?thread_ts=1681136821.761299&cid=C03UY0T0WV7|smart-link]); it’s not yet clear if approver will be a person or a team, and if it’s a specific person then maybe just having Slack notifications like for backend credentials will suffice
# PR reviews – there are existing integrations for it, but it’s worth noticing that the flow is similar
# Engineering Tax & Debt projects and Engineering-wide announcements – here we notify about upcoming changes or migrations that will have to be performed by teams in {{#foundation-announcements}}, but it’s mostly up to teams to keep track of those. There is a Jira project for [https://taxify.atlassian.net/jira/software/c/projects/ETD/boards/620|https://taxify.atlassian.net/jira/software/c/projects/ETD/boards/620|smart-link], but not sure if it covers all of such announcements. Here we could also go back to the idea of having to explicitly mark announcements as read, so that we could be sure that important announcements aren’t missed, and we could remind about unread announcements (e.g. to GTLs) on regular basis.

It is quite possible that this is a mix of very different scenarios, but the general idea is that it would be beneficial to have a single dashboard for each Engineering team where they would see all their pending tasks, so that it would be clear what’s expected from them, in other words – for visibility. Maybe part of this will be handled by Review & Approval system, where we could show pending tasks per team/person. Maybe it’s ok to have different mechanisms for different systems and types of reminders and actionables, but having a single dashboard to unify those integrations still sounds beneficial.

Having a team dashboard would also add a possibility to reach out to the team in case they misconfigured their Slack channel, because right now our best option is to write on Github team’s page which is rarely used and checked by anyone.

{noformat}select 
  city_id
  , date_trunc('hour',time_window_start) as utc_hour
  , date_trunc('hour',time_window_start_local) as local_hour
  , sum(state_duration_seconds) as paid_time_seconds
from dbt_silja_mardla_spark.driver_order_state_durations
where city_id=1
and is_paid=1
group by 
    city_id
  , date_trunc('hour',time_window_start)
  , date_trunc('hour',time_window_start_local)
order by city_id, utc_hour{noformat}



{noformat}--2 hours ahead of utc on march 16
select 
    city_id
  , period_local as local_hour
  , sum(paid_time_seconds)
from ng_public_spark.etl_driver_hourly_activity
where date(period_local_date) = date('2023-03-16')
and city_id = 1
and period_local >= timestamp('2023-03-16 00:00')
and period_local < timestamp('2023-03-17 00:00')
group by
    city_id
  , period_local
order by city_id, period_local{noformat}

Please see below the assessment for Norway. 

# *Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied?*
Yes. It is quite common for independent contractors to file lawsuits alleging misclassification, claiming de facto employment with the engaging entity under the Norwegian Working Environment Act (section 1-8).
# *Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)* 
The authorities closely scrutinise independent contractor arrangements and staffing platforms. There is also significant public, political, and media attention on this topic. Similar platforms, such as Uber and Foodora, have faced various claims in recent years. For example, Foodora now employs all personnel and is bound by a collective bargaining agreement.
# *Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria?*
Yes. In order to be considered as an independent contractor – and not a "de facto" employee – the following main criteria apply:
- A contractor should (at least be able to) take on assignments for more than one company
- A contractor should use his/her own tools and/or equipment (in this case, car);
- A contractor should be responsible for his/her work performance;
- A contractor should not be subject to the instructions etc. of the company;
- A contractor's fee/remuneration will often be fixed for the complete assignment and not based on hours spent etc.

A concrete overall assessment must be made based on the abovementioned main criteria in order to determine whether the individual may be considered an independent contractor.

Please note that the government recently adopted amendments to the legislation regarding the classification of employees and independent contractors, intending to make it easier for contractors to determine whether they are entitled to employee status under the law. Effective 1 January 2024, the definition of "employee" will be changed to "anyone who performs work for and is subordinate to another". Furthermore, a presumption rule will be introduced stating that employee status should be assumed unless the contractor can demonstrate that a contractual relationship (rather than an employment relationship) is "overwhelmingly likely". As a result, the engaging entities will be required to provide strong evidence of a contractual relationship. Failure to meet the evidential standard will result in the contractor being classified as an employee.
# *Are reclassification sensitive activities expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?* 
In cases of misclassification claims, the courts will conduct a full examination of the reality of the relationship between the parties in light of the mentioned main criteria. The courts place specific emphasis on the control and influence of the engaging entity, who bears the risk of the work result and the individual's need for protection.
# *Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)*
If the company is deemed the de facto employer of the individual(s) in question, the individuals may be entitled to holiday pay and pension contributions dating back at least three years. In addition, the company might be liable for employers' social contribution (payroll tax), withholding tax on salary, additional penalty charges on employers' social contribution and penal sanctions.
# *Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators*
In Norway, both individual drivers and groups of drivers may take legal action before the courts against Bolt if they believe they are misclassified as independent contractors. Regulators may also impose public law sanctions such as orders and administrative fines if they consider Bolt to have violated Norwegian employment law.
# *Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?*
We do not know the specifics of the case against Uber, but we understand the investigation, inter alia, focused on regulatory approval and tax issues.
# *What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?* 
In Norway, the justice system is generally considered accessible. The courts generally consider individuals as the weaker party in the relationship with the platform entities and will often be inclined to judge in favour of the weaker party.

Further, in employment-related disputes, efforts are made to reduce costs and streamline the legal process by encouraging parties to participate in mediation before the main hearing. In this form of settlement negotiations, a judge will facilitate the communication and negotiation between the parties with the goal of reaching a mutually agreeable solution. Furthermore, the employer is rarely awarded full legal costs in employment-related disputes, which makes the legal system more accessible to employees.

Additionally, Norwegian workers have the right to join trade unions, which can provide legal support and representation in employment-related cases. Trade unions have a strong presence in Norway and are considered an important part of the labour market. Union membership is relatively high in Norway in certain sectors, and the topic of reclassification is a focus of the unions.
# *Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers of the platform in a market at once?*
In principle, yes, but this requires that all employees participate in a class action. While such claims are unprecedented in Norway, we have seen litigation involving numerous employees simultaneously. If such a claim is made successfully, this will likely imply that the same classification applies to all personnel, given the limited differences between the individuals in this context.

As you can see the responses are similar as the responses for Sweden but I want to note that trade unions also play a vital role in Sweden as they do in Norway (this was not mentioned in my comments before). 

I will revert with responses for Finland. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Adding some more information I received from Tiiu. Helena Rachao posted something like this a while ago:

_Do the existing rules for driver reporting remain in place and run in parallel to the DAC7 reporting or will these rules be abolished with the DAC7 taking effect from 1 January 2023 onwards?_

* No reporting requirements would apply in France in relation to underlying transactions carried out as of 1 January 2023, except the one consisting in informing service providers of their possible French social and fiscal obligations upon each transaction. What does this exception actually mean? # Are there any risks for Bolt to issue the requested waivers to ROFR?

# The RoFR and the call option right have not been validly created, particularly because they were not granted by the Shareholders. Consequently, *_these rights are not "enforceable"_* as such under Hungarian law.

# The RoFR Agreement appears to regulate only the *_direct_* transfer of the shares in the Hungary Partner, if the restructuring were implemented, in the case of subsequent transfers of the shares in the New Shareholders (i.e. "indirect transfers") Bolt would no longer be able to argue that the Partner's “procure” obligation has been breached.
# Additional securities are as follows:

* New RoFR and Call Option Agreement is signed, where Bolt’s rights are granted directly (as contracting parties) by the direct owners of the shares in Hungary Partner (current shareholders and new shareholders after restructuring);
* Further transfer of shares (including indirect change of control) is restricted, and change of control provisions are added to the RoFR agreement;
* Bolt's rights should also be incorporated in the constitutional documents of the Hungary Partner (articles of association, register of shareholders);

Ok, quick rough numbers. 
this is what i managed to flag from replicating the example from these orders.
Drivers that do not log the destination change but still drive more than the estimated route, meaning not following the app, having increase of price and distance from estimated to final by 2x and finishing very far from the estimated location. 
I managed to flag around 4K orders rounding up to 33K EUR. Time range 1 month.
Now the issue here is, these are cash orders and the only thing i have to go on, for considering them bad or good is the reports and comments. And the reality is, not many are reported. If we go by the data from these 4K orders only 76 have reports. It is tricky now to make a decision what level of these is fraud and what not. 
We can limit some excess thresholds (i would go into overcharge of 3 or 5 times estimated to final price and very far distances from estimated location) to hit the extreme abusers of this. Otherwise we will just hurt the GMV, making a decision on data that is not complete. 
The solution we have in mind is price recalculation. If an order like this is flagged, the price will be recalculated back to the estimated one, so the drivers are losing the incentive to abuse this overcharge. But this relies heavily on the instruction to CS to not compensate drivers afterwards. Global instructions have been sent to CS but let’s see how it will go in practice. 
But if regulatory requirements are involved and they state that this should not happen at all (cus fraud can flag some top abusers, can’t stop 100% of the behaviour) then i would suggest those requirements to be raised to product side or to pricing so these recalculations or rides are prevented automatically.

# Партнер пропонує, щоб ми були відповідальними за дії кур'єрів і відшкодовували їм збитки у випадку невиконання кур'єрами договору про доставку. # Партнер пропонує вносити зміни до Загальних умов - наші Загальні умови розроблені на основі глобальної версії таких Загальних умов, яка використовується з необхідними змінами у всіх країнах, де Bolt здійснює діяльність. Всі партнери, окрім критичних партнерів, які мають власні проекти договорів (напр. Макдональдс) приймають такі Загальні умови і використовують наші послуги на їх основі. Відповідно, за загальним правилом зміни у Загальні умови ми не вносимо. У критичних випадках, ми можемо додати таблицю до Спеціальних умов, де викладемо необхідні зміни до Загальних умов, але це робити небажано.
# Ми не можемо підписати даний протокол розбіжностей і вважати, що договір укладено. З партнером мають бути підписані спеціальні умови з необхідними погодженими змінами за загальним порядком. Тому даний протокол наразі є лише проектом, де відображені майбутні зміни до стандартного проекту спеціальних умов.

h2. Reusable solution for reimporting images for a menu

{code:sql}-- (1) If you're starting from providers, first get the list of menus & vendors
select
    distinct b.vendor_id, a.menu_id
from
    provider_active_menu a
inner join
    menu_version b on a.menu_id = b.menu_id
where
    a.provider_id in (46405, 48838, 53476, 46818, 46822, 46823, 53477, 53478, 56696, 46824, 47150, 53474, 53475, 64953);

-- (2) Configure the parameters below
select @reason := 'https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/DPM-816';
select @vendor_id := 32412;
select @menu_id := 1765068173;

-- (3) For each menu & vendor pair do:

-- (3.1) Start a new transaction
begin;

-- (3.2) Set to 'pending' rows from menu_item_image
with menu_item_image_ids as
    (
    select 
        distinct b.id
    from
        menu_item a
    inner join
        menu_item_image b on b.image_url_crc = CRC32(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(params, "$.images[0].source_info.url")))
    where
        a.menu_id = @menu_id
        and b.vendor_id = @vendor_id
        and a.params like '%source_info%'
    )
update
    menu_item_image a
inner join
    menu_item_image_ids b on a.id = b.id
set
    a.state = 'pending',
    a.tries_no = 0,
    a.scheduled_timestamp = NOW(),
    a.reason = @reason
where
    a.id > 0 -- so that MySQL Workbench allows executing this query
;

-- (3.3) Insert new jobs in menu_item_image_job
insert into menu_item_image_job(
    menu_item_id,
    menu_item_image_id,
    menu_id,
    priority,
    state,
    scheduled_timestamp,
    reason
)
select 
    a.id, -- menu_item_id
    b.id, -- menu_item_image_id
    a.menu_id, -- menu_id
    3, -- priority
    'pending', -- state
    NOW(), -- scheduled_timestamp
    @reason -- reason
from
    menu_item a
inner join
    menu_item_image b on b.image_url_crc = CRC32(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(params, "$.images[0].source_info.url")))
where
    a.menu_id = @menu_id
    and b.vendor_id = @vendor_id
    and a.params like '%source_info%'
;

-- (3.4)
commit;

-- (4) To monitor use the queries below
select max(id) into @maxid from menu_item_image_job;
select row_count() into @num_inserted;

select state, reason, count(*)
from menu_item_image_job
where id between @maxid - @num_inserted and @maxid
group by state, reason;
{code}

Hi Team,

We got the response from external counsel in Latvia on possible usage of dash-board cameras in Latvia. Please see full advice attached, key take-aways are as follows:

* local legislation doesn’t prohibit using dash-board cameras, provided that privacy measures are implemented and followed;
* the processing should be documented in a form of a legitimate interest assessment (this has been done already);
* local regulator hasn’t issued a list of specific measures that need to be implemented to install the cameras, therefore I’d suggest to follow our global recommendations which include:
** no real-time monitoring -  the recordings should be only used in justified cases where we have a Bolt Drive T&C-s violations or an accident happens which requires investigation.
** there has to be a retention rule for automated recurring deletion of this data (at a point where it is no longer required).
** sensible access management rules to recordings must be abided. The internal policy is [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ISO/pages/1885077541/Access+Control+Policy], if specific support is needed, please reach out to Information Security Team.
** the user is notified about the camera in the vehicle (e.g by a sticker on a window/somewhere visible in and on the car).
** if the plan is to use dual cameras (even if the inside of the vehicle is not recorded) the front facing camera should be taped (so that the user understands that no monitoring is taking place), it is placed behind the mirror and no memory card is installed.

Also, please note that our current Privacy Notice for Bolt Drive in LV already covers potential usage of cameras, so no need to amend it.

Please let me know if you have any additional questions on this.

Kind regards,

Adriana

There are 3 different types of terminations for option grants:

||*During cliff period*||*Good Leaver*||*Bad leaver*||
|If employee leaves before passing cliff period (usually their first year) then as they haven’t vested anything until that point, there will be no units for them to keep and their whole grant will be terminated fully|If employee has passed their cliff period and is declared a good leaver then they will keep all vested units, and all unvested units will be returned to Bolt’s Option Pool. All employees leaving the company will be considered as Good leavers, unless indicated otherwise!

The EU VAT legislation does not prescribe the use of any language. Estonia VAT regulations are based on EU VAT regulations and, in this regard, article 37 of EE KMS (which governs invoicing for EE VAT purposes) does not impose the obligation to issue invoices in Estonian.

Notwithstanding the above, I would like to share two considerations:

# Perhaps there is a Law in EE governing consumers’ rights. I would look into such legislation because I think that it may provide for the right of Estonian individual consumers to get an invoice in Estonian.
# Thinking as an owner, I think it makes sense to provide local customers (especially if they are private individuals) with invoices issued in their language, as the main purpose of any invoice, voucher or receipt is to let the addressee know (in a clear and understandable manner) about the concept and the reason behind a payment or a charge in their bank account or credit card.

From my POV, the ideal solution may be to issue invoices in the local language and in English, so that they can be understood by any Bolt member who might need to check any given transaction or whose work has to do with invoices (i.e. VAT compliance).

Thank you. Have a good day.

Hello Emmanuel!

Please be advised that the topic and process of destination changes were discussed and confirmed with your Country Manager. We would like to understand better what has led you to believe these are completed incorrectly. Have you proposed and confirmed a new process with your CM? On the fraud side, we have not received any requests for process changes or updates from your country management for fraud price reviews or logic. We would also like to request more information on your claim that the destinations are left in the comments. Have the users been advised to do so? What has led to this practice?

Let me give a bit of information on why comments do not equal destination changes. Each step in order has its own line of decisions and checks. This means that if there is an order request, we always run a check on if this is an acceptable request. These checks range from safety to fraud to availability - meaning there are numerous small decisions that are confirmed for the ride to happen. The same goes for any updates to destinations or multiple-stop journeys: these small checks run to see if the request is legitimate and can be allowed with our company’s and users' security and best interests at heart. As the same does not happen for leaving comments (which is just driver-rider communication/interaction), this practice does not equal the same as updating destinations through the app or adding these before the journey. 

In general, the drivers have to be educated on the flow of the app and to log all changes. There will be instructions provided for the driver based on the checks and decisions as stated above. [For further reference, please check this out.|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7643088163474] However, most importantly, logging all destinations is significant due to Bolt being held liable in the end. Without logging destinations through the app and receiving approval from us, it is just a direct interaction between the rider and the driver which goes against our whole concept, licencing and responsibilities. 

Awaiting to hear from you,

*Summary for app version verification:*
Right now we have app version validation in _/driver/geLoggedInConfiguration_ endpoint, which is called right after the driver logs in to the app (_auth → /driver/getAccessToken → /driver/geLoggedInConfiguration_).
I propose to do this verification in _/driver/getAccessToken_ endpoint and encrypt the app version to access token. This approach gives us the possibility to get a ‘valid’ app version during the execution of any endpoint for driver flow without calling fleet API to get ‘valid' app version. We can create a new driver auth strategy that will compare the app version from the access token to one that is passed in query parameters (using [postCheckAuth|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/c75ac52485300f952eb9b6af74b67d02f22961cd/common/delivery/router/async/DeliveryCourierAuthStrategy.ts#L21]). So this new driver auth strategy can be used in 'core’ endpoints, where do we think third-party cloned apps can pass old app versions in query params to bypass some of our features (driver score).

Hi Valid, 

Apologies for the delay. I can put it this way for you: 

The fraud team is responsible for triggering and/or suggesting which users need verification and we start the flow of requesting one, such as for this user. However, once we have “asked” the verification system/flow to start, we do not have the ability or authority to adjust anything. Once verification as the owner of the flow completes with the user, the fraud flow gets the message of what was the result. If the result is negative, we don’t offer a new automatic flow. 

However, here the answer is inconclusive rather than negative meaning that if they try to place another order, the same process should be offered - such as for the last multiple attempts. 

BUT now what has made us suggest a consultation with the I&V team, is the repetitive unsuccessful attempts. Why can’t the user complete the verification? Have they been advised on the quality? So, make sure you have advised the user before they attempt a new one or consult the verification team about any concerns within the process that can affect the user’s ability to follow through. 

Alternatively, there is a general [manual verification process too|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360018988839] you may want to try out for this user. 

Hope this helps & we are here if you need any further advice.

# Звітний період пропонуємо зробити з 1-го по 15-е число та з 15-го по останнє число кожного місяця.

*_Такий підхід не є можливим, оскільки вся система налаштована на тижневий період в усіх країнам, де працює Болт - всі розрахунки, інвойси, звіти по продажам, Звіти агента формуються на тижневій основі - за результатами роботи з понеділка по неділю._*

2. Ви нам сплачуєте повну суму за замовленні товари два рази на місяць. Агентські послуги не утримуються. Так як після кожного періоду необхідно проводити звірку. 

*_Відповідь у п.1. + Для звірки партнер може використовувати звіти по продажам, що надходитимуть щопонеділка на пошту - там будуть всі виконані замовлення у розрізі днів, обсяг продажів, нарахована комісія, маркетингові вивтрати за підключені промо акції (якщо будуть). Виконані замовлення вже не коригуються - вони автоматично потрапляють у тижневі продажі партнера і виплату. Єдине в чому можуть бути розбіжності - компенсації за переприготування замовлень. Ці суми можна буде коригувати._*

3. Звірку проводимо по електронній пошті. У вас є реєстри замовлень, які ви зможете нам направляти? Звіт (або реєстр) ми маємо отримувати на наступний робочий день після закінчення звітного періоду. Після цього обмінюємось актами. 

*_Див. п.2 - щопонеділка партнеру на пошту приходить звіт по продажам - перелік всіх замовлень у розрізі днів, які реалізовані через платформу. Додатково ще можна користуватися Порталом для ректоранів - корисутватися Деталізованими звітами, Історією замовлень._*

4. Агентські послуги ми вам сплачуємо окремо теж два рази на місяць після звірки. Платимо (ми і ви) протягом 7 (семи) робочих днів після звірки. 

*_Щопонеділка ми перераховуємо партнеру всі продажі за тиждень, партнер протягом 3-х днів оплачує нашу комісії та інші необхідні збори (маркетинг, наприклад)_*

5. Планшети ми не використовуємо. Всі дані передаються за допомогою API. Ми вам передаємо асортимент з цінами і актуальними залишками по кожній торговій точці. Ви нам передаєте інфо про підтверджені (оплачені) замовлення. Замовлення автоматично формується в нашій ERP-системі виключаючи людський фактор. 
*_Так, це можливо налаштувати за допомогою інтеграції._*

6. Штрафні санкції робимо двосторонніми. 
*_Приймаємо._*

7. Стосовно пункту 10. Вам необхідно буде реєструвати податкові накладні, так як ми будемо сплачувати вам агентські послуги. 
*_Коментар у документі._*

8. Ми не приймаємо умови, які змінюються в односторонньому порядку. Всі додаткові платежі або умови узгоджуються додатковими угодами.
*_Коментарі у документі._*

9. Опис інтеграції та технічні деталі виносимо в окрему угоду. 
*_Всі деталі (в тому числі технічні) встановлюються у Спеціальних умовах із партнером._*

10. Також нас не влаштовує ваша поточна позиція стосовно вирішення проблем з кур’єрами. Що буде, якщо кур’єр неналежним чином доставить товар: загубив, пошкодив і т.ін.? Хто в такому випадку має вирішувати проблему з клієнтом?
*_Коментарі у документі._*

SELECT 
x.count_permanent_errors,
--x.count_fraud_errors,
--x.distinct_countries_we_dont_operate,
--x.country_code,
APPROX_DISTINCT(x.user_id,0.0041) AS count_users,
SUM(x.count_orders) AS count_orders,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.sum_price_eur) AS double),0) AS sum_price_eur,
SUM(x.count_fraud_orders) AS count_fraud_orders,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.fraud_sum_price_eur) AS double),0) AS fraud_sum_price_eur,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.count_fraud_orders)*1.00/SUM(x.count_orders) AS double),2) AS fraud_ratio,
ROUND(CAST(ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.fraud_sum_price_eur) AS double),0)*1.00/ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.sum_price_eur) AS double),0) AS double),2) AS fraud_sum_ratio,
SUM(x.count_cb_orders) AS count_cb_orders,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.cb_sum_price_eur) AS double),0) AS cb_sum_price_eur,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.count_cb_orders)*1.00/SUM(x.count_orders) AS double),2) AS cb_ratio,
ROUND(CAST(ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.cb_sum_price_eur) AS double),0)*1.00/ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.sum_price_eur) AS double),0) AS double),0) AS cb_sum_ratio,
SUM(x.count_pp_orders) AS count_pp_orders,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.pp_sum_price_eur) AS double),0) AS pp_sum_price_eur,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.count_pp_orders)*1.00/SUM(x.count_orders) AS double),2) AS pp_ratio,
ROUND(CAST(ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.pp_sum_price_eur) AS double),0)*1.00/ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.sum_price_eur) AS double),0) AS double),0) AS pp_sum_ratio,
SUM(x.count_fp_orders) AS count_fp_orders,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.fp_sum_uncovered_eur) AS double),0) AS fp_sum_uncovered_eur,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.count_fp_orders)*1.00/SUM(x.count_orders) AS double),2) AS fp_ratio,
ROUND(CAST(ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.fp_sum_uncovered_eur) AS double),0)*1.00/ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.sum_price_eur) AS double),0) AS double),0) AS fp_sum_ratio
FROM (
WITH payment_instrument_info AS (
SELECT 
a.user_id,
APPROX_DISTINCT(a.id,0.0041) AS count_methods_total,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.state = 'success' THEN a.id END,0.0041) AS successful_total,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.state = 'error' THEN a.id END,0.0041) AS error_total,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN (a.error_message IN ('PAYMENT_ERROR_PERMANENT','card.blacklisted','card.invalid-account','card.invalid-number','card.security-violation','card.stolen','check.invalid-micr','PAYMENT_ERROR_INVALID_CVV','card.invalid-cvc','PAYMENT_ERROR_BLOCKED_CARD','card.lost','PAYMENT_ERROR_CARD_EXPIRED','PAYMENT_3DS1_NOT_AUTHENTICATED') OR a.raw_response_gateway IN ('card.blacklisted','card.expired','card.failed-3ds','card.failed-cvc','card.inactive','card.invalid','card.invalid-account','card.invalid-cvc','card.invalid-expiry-date','card.invalid-number','card.invalid-pin','card.law-violation','card.lost','card.not-activated','card.stolen','check.invalid-micr')) THEN a.id END,0.0041) AS count_permanent_errors,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN (a.error_message IN ('PAYMENT_ERROR_FRAUD','card.possible-fraud','gateway.possible-fraud') OR a.raw_response_gateway IN ('card.possible-counterfeit','card.possible-fraud','gateway.possible-fraud')) THEN a.id END,0.0041) AS count_fraud_errors,
-- fraud errors can also be permanent errors
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN a.state = 'created' THEN a.id END,0.0041) AS created_state_total,
APPROX_DISTINCT(lower(a.card_country),0.0041) AS distinct_countries,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN lower(a.card_country) NOT IN ('se','gb','pl','tn','lk','pt','ee','fr','za','py','sk','ro','ke','es','sa','th','ec','de','at','am','lv','iq','nl','ge','mx','cy','fi','tz','az','gh','hu','hn','cz','ua','ng','ug','mt','lb','eg','np','no','be','hr','ie','sv','lt') THEN a.card_country END,0.0041) AS distinct_countries_we_dont_operate,
APPROX_DISTINCT(lower(a.country_code),0.0041) AS distinct_adding_countries,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN lower(a.country_code) NOT IN ('se','gb','pl','tn','lk','pt','ee','fr','za','py','sk','ro','ke','es','sa','th','ec','de','at','am','lv','iq','nl','ge','mx','cy','fi','tz','az','gh','hu','hn','cz','ua','ng','ug','mt','lb','eg','np','no','be','hr','ie','sv','lt') THEN a.card_country END,0.0041) AS distinct_adding_countries_we_dont_operate
FROM ng_commerce.payment_method_etl a
WHERE a.created_date >= date '2023-02-01'
GROUP BY 1 
)
SELECT 
pi.*,
etl.country_code,
APPROX_DISTINCT(etl.order_id,0.0041) AS count_orders,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(etl.user_price_eur) AS double),2) AS sum_price_eur,
COALESCE(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN etl.fraud_label THEN etl.order_id END,0.0041),0) AS count_fraud_orders,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN etl.fraud_label THEN etl.user_price_eur END) AS double),2),0) AS fraud_sum_price_eur,

Seems that in this specific case this error might be triggered by queries timing out due to resource starvation, or, it’s just a reaction to the query cancelled due to TTL exceeded. I assume you should treat this error similar to MAX_EXECUTION_TIME timeout.

Some context:

Context cancellation in TiDB can be triggered by a variety of events. Here are some of the most common reasons why a query may be cancelled:

# User-initiated cancellation: The user who initiated the query can cancel it at any time, for example, by sending a {{KILL}} query from another session.
# Timeout: TiDB has several timeout settings that can cause a query to be cancelled if it exceeds a certain time limit. For example, the {{tidb_distsql_scan_concurrency}} setting controls the maximum amount of time that a distributed table scan can run before being cancelled.
# Resource constraints: If the query requires more resources (such as memory or CPU) than are available, it may be cancelled.
# Connection issues: If there are connection issues between the TiDB server and the client, the query may be cancelled.
# Server maintenance: If the TiDB server is taken offline for maintenance, any running queries may be cancelled.
# Query interception: In some cases, TiDB may intercept a query and cancel it before it can be executed. For example, if the query is deemed to be too expensive or too complex, TiDB's query interceptor may cancel it.

These are just a few examples of events that can trigger context cancellation in TiDB. The specific reason for cancellation can usually be found in the error message returned by the server, which will include details about the error code and message.

One reason the auto-promotion fails is the fact that we have a threshold of 100 orders to be used when getting the active cities and some cities make it one week but don’t make it the next. This would happen regardless of the threshold. This threshold is set in the {{popular-places}} job. There is another threshold of 2% missing cities in the {{model-release}} job - if more then 2% (6-7 cities) of cities are missing from the forward model, the promotion fails.
We have decided for now to let the job as it is, and revisit this task if it fails constantly.

We will fix it by:

As for recommendations:

# “Ensure that the application sufficiently validates a user’s access against their intended role” - insofar as the {{device_id}} and {{device_name}} params are *not used* for identification, this can be considered resolved.
Note if these do become sensitive, we will not have a viable strategy for BYOD devices where {{device_id}} and {{device_name}} are determined by the device. We’d need to somehow collect these during the registration process (which is not automated) and then ensure that as the provider changes devices, they are also kept up to date. For now I think it is far too expensive compared to what it achieves.
#  “Do not rely on easily discoverable information for checking access levels.” - I don’t think we do this at the moment (where possible).
# “Ensure sensitive data is sent via the POST requests body, and not within the URL  parameters.” - Even if {{device_name}} suddenly becomes sensitive, moving the params will not come for free. Not only do we need to migrate almost all of our endpoints, we also need to change the app’s default param strategy where applicable.
Sounds reasonable to try to address this.

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2], please see information below regarding Finland. 

*General overview*

In short, there have been recent legislative changes to alleviate the difficulty relating to the assessment whether a contractual relationship is employment or not and a recent proposal to allow workers easy access to have their status assessed but this proposal is at its early stages. In addition, as we have a quite recent, legally non-binding classification decisions regarding Wolt couriers, one could say the topic concerning platform workers is getting noticed more than before but still I would say we’re far behind with this compared to some other countries in Europe or the US.

What we lack is clear legislation and binding court decisions regarding the status of platform workers. Existing court decisions concern other types of workers and their status as either an employee or entrepreneur. What makes the situation even more confusing is that our tax authorities seem to have more flexible view on the platform workers than bodies that assess the situation from purely employment law perspective.

The authority that has shown most interest in the topic is the Health and Safety Authority and it remains to be seen whether they are taking more active role in defining the status of platform workers as so far it seems this has not been a priority topic for any authority or body.

*Questions*

# *Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied?*
Yes. Chapter 1 Section 1 of the Finnish Employment Contracts Act defines the criteria upon which employment relationship shall be assessed and considered. Employment relationship is established if a person works personally on behalf of the employer, under the employer’s supervision and direction and against remuneration. The assessment will overall assessment. Only the fact that the employee works at a place of the employee’s choice or uses his/her own working tools and devices does not rule out the application of the Employment Contracts Act.
# *Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc)*
The Health and Safety Authority has been investigating the contractual relationship of couriers of Wolt. Upon the Authority’s request, the Labour Council rendered its decision on whether the couriers should be reclassified as employees. The decision was in favor of the couriers and set some guidance on under which circumstances the couriers shall be considered as employees. However, the decision is not legally binding but naturally the decision will have relevance in a possible court process even though the court must assess a case independently and based on the facts presented in court. There are no court rulings regarding reclassification of platform workers so far but there are recent court cases regarding reclassification of other types of workers. In addition, the wording of the Section of the Employment Contracts Act referred to in our answer to question 1 was recently slightly amended and the purpose was to alleviate the assessment of an employment relationship.
# *Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria?*
Not to similar presumption criteria as set out in the proposal for the EU Directive concerning platform workers.
# *Are reclassification sensitive activities expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?*
There are no specific laws, courts or bodies expressly considering reclassification issues but the Health and Safety Authority has shown interested on reclassification sensitive activities and not only from the health and safety perspective but reclassification perspective which is within the scope of their authorities. In addition, the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment has initiated a research to investigate how to arrange easy access to workers to have their contractual relationship assessed and potentially reclassified. This initiative is only on its early stages and there are no concrete proposals yet.
# *Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?)*
Yes. Employee claims relating to unpaid salary (such as overtime or mandatory salary increases) can extend up to past five years and claims relating to loss of holidays up to two years. Tax authority may also extend their claims regarding unpaid taxes and social security payments up to past five years and impose additional fines for neglecting mandatory employer obligations. The pension authority may decide to arrange for pension insurance for employees in case the employer does not arrange pension insurance upon the authority’s order. The pension authority may also impose an additional negligence fee amounting to 10-30 % of the unpaid pension payments.
# *Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators.*
Each employee individually. In addition, the Health and Safety Authority may also investigate the employment terms and status of the workers either at their own initiative or upon request of an employee. The Health and Safety Authority can either give instructions and guidance for the employer about arranging the employments or it can ask for a decision from the Labour Council on the contractual status of the workers. It is up to the employer to decide whether it acts on the basis of the decision of the Labour Council if the decision would be in favor of the workers and reclassify them as employees. Furthermore, the tax and pension authorities may investigate at their own initiative whether an employer has complied with its mandatory employer obligations.
# *Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)?*
In relation to platform workers, we’re not aware of such decisions but this kind of decisions would not become public unless the employing company appeals to a court and the court decision is published. In relation other workers than platform workers, there have been decisions where the authorities have ordered the employer to pay unpaid taxes and social security payments retrospectively. One peculiarity in the Finnish system is that different bodies and authorities may give conflicting decisions. Even though the Labour Council and the Health and Safety Authority reclassified the Wolt couriers as employees, and also the Finnish Workers' Compensation Center considered the couriers should be insured with mandatory employee accident insurance, an Administrative Court rendered a decision that a Wolt courier was obliged to pay VAT because the courier was not an employee but an entrepreneur.
# *What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)?* 
The level of access to justice is rather high as there’s no requirement for having legal representative. If an employee files a application for summons to a district court without resorting to legal assistance and if the employee’s summons is inadequate, the court has an obligation to give the employee some guidance by asking questions so that the employee can complete the summons and continue process. A person with no adequate means to litigate may be eligible for legal aid from the state. Furthermore, authorities, such as the Health and Safety authority, have a duty to give an employee guidance in their legal matters free of charge but the authority cannot file a claim on behalf of the employee. In our assessment, resorting to the assistance of the Health and Safety Authority may be the most likely option for a worker at the moment.
# *Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers of the platform in a market at once?*
The Labour Council can render a decision that will apply to all employees who fall within the scope of the decision. If the Health and Safety Authority brings a case for the Council to assess, the Authority must describe the circumstances of the workers and their working terms and the Council will base its decision on these facts. The employer in question will be given a chance to respond to the request made by the Authority and comment on the Authority’s view about the potential reclassification. However, as stated, it is up to the employer to decide whether it will change its business model and reclassify the platform workers as employees. Otherwise, for now, there’s no procedure on how to get all drivers reclassified at once but each worker would need to file a claim in court.

Let me know if you have any follow-up questions. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

So to clarify the current set-up the following happens: 

* If the driver recovers the costs from the passenger directly, e.g. by cash payment or transfer, and the passenger then reaches out to Bolt we will inform the driver that they need to repay the amount and the driver is blocked. These are the guidelines from global risk & safety team apparently and this is obviously not in line with what we have in our T&Cs. This means that basically the driver knows that if they try to recover the cost then they are blocked from the platform. 
* Drivers should request a price review and provide an invoice of the cleaning service. 
* Bolt will then charge the passenger and this will be done directly from the primary payment method. 

The issue with this is that a lot of the drivers clean their cars themselves but they still want to receive reimbursement for this and the time that they couldn’t accept any rides because they were spending the time cleaning instead. Therefore, drivers have submitted fake invoices instead so in order to avoid this, the RH team requested that we introduce specific amounts that the passenger will be charged for in case of specific damages (basically an increasing ladder based on how bad the damage is). 

When we discussed this for SE the suggestion was to issue the invoices for cleaning services to the passengers on behalf of drivers, and not on behalf of Bolt. Bolt would simply act as an assistant for fine mediation on behalf of driver as we do with the transportation service. We would also phrase it accordingly in our Rider T&Cs. However, we have not implemented this yet due to heavy workload but that is the latest suggestion but I do believe we should align on this on our markets [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] so we follow the same approach.

I may suggest the following procedure (points 1 and 2 in next steps). If you have any questions and or if I have been unclear, please contact me at any time. 

*I. Background:* In the context of data processing for the provision of shared mobility services (eScooter, eBike, CarSharing) there were 2 decisions last year (both in France, but with involvement of data protection authorities in Germany, Italy and Spain) regarding the excessive collection and use of user data *(It may be pointed out  that from a data protection point of view not only obvious personal data such as name, address, telephone number, but also data such as location data of a scooter, speed, parking behavior,.. are considered as personal data if this data can be assigned to a user (e.g.: A scooter moves from A to B, if this movement can be assigned to a user by Bolt (even if only internally and with additional effort) it is his personal data).*

Competitors have put forward convincing arguments (safety, protection against theft, etc.), and the supervisory authority has accepted some of these arguments as justification. Nevertheless, the authority assumed excessive processing in some cases as well. 

*II.* *Aim:* The aim of the survey is not to immediately restrict processing, but to collect what data is being processed and stored and to what extent, *to evaluate and identify potential risks***  and to work together to minimise those risks.* 

*III. Procedure:* as already mentioned, the concept of personal data is very broad. It is therefore requested to {color:#ff5630}*provide the following information:*{color}

* Information that is collected by MobilDevice in the context of eScooter/eBike-rentals (eg. UserID, Longitude Phone, Latitude phone, UserFeedback, Picture parked scooter...).
* Information that is ycollected from the rental vehicle as part of the eScooter/eBike-rental-service (eg.ScooterID, longitude scooter, latitude scooter, charge, speed,...)
* Information created during the provision of the scooter service (order specific info like OrderId, journey, pick up, drop off, pricing, distance,...)
* Data collected/processed for special processing activities (Tandem Riding, Drink Drive Prevention, GroupRides, park assistant,…)

Hi [~accountid:61c450c9f3037f006962ddd1] - again, thanks for your patience on this.

I suspect that Uber are running this for publicity, rather than anything they intend to do long term. 

You ask the right question: _how does this impact ‘reclassification’?_

As you may know, in the UK Uber treats its drivers as ‘workers’, which is a different type of engagement than how Uber operates elsewhere and how Bolt treats its drivers globally, which is as ‘independent contractors’.

Childcare-type benefits are typically associated with employment-like relationships. Uber is already treating its drivers as workers in the UK, which (speaking generally) is a “semi-employee” status, so this is not such an issue for Uber. However, unlike Uber, Bolt’s own narrative that it is *_not_* engaging with drivers in a controlling, employment-like way. 

It’s an interesting idea, but ultimately I think offering childcare-type benefits would cut across Bolt’s existing narrative. It could also be damaging to link this benefit with performance targets, as that could be used to suggest Bolt is imposing power over its drivers. 

For that reason, I do not think that this is something that Bolt should look to implement *_unless_* it was considered a business critical incentive, in which case the-local country management would need to take a view on it and consider it specifically on a market by market basis. I expect this is not business critical, rather ‘just an idea’ from looking at Uber’s operations. Perhaps the appropriate time to revisit this would be if Uber starts launching this in western EU countries.

Types of incentives that are much more in line with Bolt’s existing model are typical payment campaigns (i.e. do X journeys get Y payment).

Objective is to determine legal framework around window shopping (price and ETA extractions) for specific country. Here is the methodology we launched: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/17p7di_6cr-xDO3r_VK7JWSwTpbarmzauACyTJzXOZmk/edit#heading=h.c9p5szxxk3db|https://docs.google.com/document/d/17p7di_6cr-xDO3r_VK7JWSwTpbarmzauACyTJzXOZmk/edit#heading=h.c9p5szxxk3db|smart-link] There is also section about legal risk in the methodology. For determining the legal framework the legal council should do following:

* Country legal council  uses [+Legal questionnaire+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-ZjNVX9rtsXA4IWpYt5PR3RVGLfNBY46OdpE7JGvy5g/edit] and checks following: 
** criminal punishment scope for specific country
** civil punishment scope for specific country 
** competitor T&C review
** etc
* Country legal council uses answers to questionnaire to define punishment scope for each window shopping scenario in the [+global risk matrix+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_eWb4mN9Nph8g1OuD0urnNoYmaPGjHEwlKYIMw3KfCU/edit]:
** Punishment scope will be considered every time. But if the  likelihood of the risk materializing is *LOW* than we will not ask about punishment. 

Please let me know if additional questions 🙂

Like I mentioned before. In 95% of the warehouses, or actually the premises we rent, are part of larger facilities. Therefore, it is not possible to change the owner of the meter and without having an agreement in a given location for the power consumption point as Bolt Services PL, we cannot negotiate or outsource negotiations because we have no legal basis to do so. In the case of buildings where there are several or a dozen tenants, the owner re-invoices the costs of consumed electricity to companies renting the premises. So we are not able to include all of our warehouses into this contract but we will recommend our LL companies providing such services like EIDOS and also we will ask for renewable energy certificates from them. 

I've already talked with Bolt Market manager and we will include to this contract our stores from beginning of 2024.

Hello [~accountid:6061907490e3950069a3a5d3], good morning,

Here are some general thoughts for us to initiate this debate:

# WhatsApp can access everyone’s address book data (e.g., first name, last name, mobile number, landline number - home and/or business - and email). If a company uses WhatsApp, it encourages users to share other people’s numbers with WhatsApp/Facebook/Meta. This means we could be deemed as a joint controller of personal data.
# Thinking from the perspective of a WhatsApp user (our drivers), they would also be sharing the personal data of contacts which eventually have no prior relationship with WhatsApp and unwittingly give information about themselves to the app. Since this sharing would be done because we are incentivizing them to use the app, we could also attract the joint controllership situation to us.
# If one of our users exercises any GDPR rights, are we, as a company, ready to fulfill these rights while using WhatsApp?
# WhatsApp shares data with Meta, and this implies international transfers of personal data to the US, which is currently problematic (to say the least).
# People using it (both inside and outside Bolt) can potentially create backups of their conversations in their iCloud/Google Drive personal accounts, as well as save attachments of any kind on their device’s internal or external memory, which means we lose control of personal data processed by Meta on our behalf.
# In 2021 WhatsApp was fined 225 million euros, and in 2023 was fined another 5.5 million euros and was ordered to bring its processing operations into compliance with the GDPR within six months.

In an initial way, I would say that if Bolt was going to use WhatsApp to send miscellaneous messages, there might even be possibilities to use the tool. However, considering the purpose indicated in the other ticket, i.e., interaction with our drivers and, on top of that, sending documents that, if violated, could have consequences for Bolt and for the drivers themselves, I believe it is not a good option.

Are you interested in creating a general recommendation for the company? We can do this together if you like.
